title: notme tenancy modes — "both topologies, operator-set" per ADR-0030 hybrid model (sub-bead of cloister-f289c8)
description:
## Why this bead exists

Resolves `cloister-db99cd` (notme co-locate vs external) under ADR-0030's multi-workerd hybrid model. Operator disposition (2026-06-21): **notme can be both — it can be inter-cluster, inter-service, or user-to-service identity, and the mode is a deployment setting.**

This bead carries the implementation of "both topologies, configurable per deployment."

## The three binding modes the operator can pick

Under ADR-0030's multi-workerd substrate with hybrid co-location:

| Mode | Shape | When it fits |
|---|---|---|
| **co-located trusted-tier** | notme runs as a `Bundle.kind.workerd` Worker inside router's workerd process | OSS-launch default. `docker run cloister` = working identity + gateway in one image. Hot-path lease verify is zero-copy. |
| **separate workerd (external)** | notme runs as its own workerd-class process / container (current shape) | Multi-tenant production posture. Independent scaling, independent release cycle, separate IAM. |
| **per-tenant workerd** | notme runs as one of the tenants under ADR-0030's `[[tenants]]` declaration | When a deployment treats notme-the-identity-service AS a tenant of the substrate (rare; emerges for hosted multi-org deployments) |

The substrate must support all three. Operator picks via cluster.toml.

## What ships

1. **notme `bundle build` task** — notme's TS compiled to embeddable JS (`dist/notme-bundle.js`) suitable for cloister's workerd config to `embed`. Sibling bead to file in notme repo.
2. **`cluster.capnp` variant set** — `art-default-bundled` (co-located) + `art-default-split` (external; current) + `art-default-tenant` (per-tenant workerd, future). The schema already reserves `Bundle.kind.workerd`; the variants pick which kind notme uses.
3. **`config.capnp`** gains a second Worker entry conditionally (when bundled variant is selected).
4. **`scripts/emit-compose.mjs` + `scripts/cluster-dev.mjs`** detect the variant and behave correctly (only cloister-router subprocess for bundled, mac-dev launcher elides notme entry).
5. **`docs/deployment/cluster-in-a-pod.md`** "Three topologies" section.
6. **ADR amendment** to ADR-0009 (Phase 1) OR fresh ADR — TBD which. The decision routes through `cloister-f289c8`'s supervisor-1 + routing-1 implementation work because the cluster.toml `[[tenants]]` table is the operator surface.

## Operator surface (provisional)

```toml
[[tenants]]
name = "notme-identity"
mode = "co-located"          # | "external" | "per-tenant"
workerd_id = "cloister-router"  # only for co-located; the workerd that hosts the bundle
```

## Coordinated with

- **Parent epic**: `cloister-f289c8` (multi-workerd substrate, vault first)
- **ADR-0030** §D4 (hybrid model)
- **ADR-0013** (slice-grant; co-located trusted-tier still V8-isolate-separated from non-trusted bundles)
- **ADR-0009** Phase 1 (cluster-in-a-pod substrate)
- **Cross-repo**: notme repo needs the bundle-build task before any variant lands

## Acceptance

- Three topology variants expressible in cluster.capnp / cluster.toml
- Operator sets the mode via cluster.toml setting
- All three boot via `task cluster:up`
- `scripts/integration-test.sh` (per `cloister-1b1124`) exercises at least the co-located + external variants
- ADR ratifies the three-topology disposition
- notme-side sibling bead files the bundle-build work

## Status

Open. Filed 2026-06-21 to capture `cloister-db99cd`'s disposition under ADR-0030's hybrid model. Implementation scope is substantial (~half-day to a day for the substrate side; cross-repo coordination for notme bundle build). Blocks on `cloister-f289c8`'s schema-1 (cluster.toml `[[tenants]]` shape) landing first.

comments.text:
**Resolved — folded into compose-emitter 2026-06-22** (commit 947881b on origin/main).

The "both topologies, operator-set" disposition (your direction in fire 4) is now fully expressible via the ADR-0030 §A5 composition model:

```toml
[inputs.notme]
ref     = "github://agentic-research/notme@<SHA>"
version = "^0.1"

  [inputs.notme.tenancy]
  mode              = "co-located"          # OSS-launch default
  workerdId         = "cloister-router"
  trustedTier       = true
  sharesWorkerdWith = []
```

OR `mode = "external"` for separate-container topology, OR `mode = "per-tenant"` for multi-tenant production (when vault-1 lands the substrate primitive).

The compose emitter walks the `[inputs.*].tenancy.*` declarations and produces the matching service shape. Documented in `docs/deployment/cluster-in-a-pod.md §"Tenancy modes (ADR-0030 §A5)"` with a worked notme example.

Cross-repo coordination remains: notme repo needs the `bundle build` task before `mode = "co-located"` can actually wire a Worker into cloister-router's workerd config. That work is **out of this bead's scope** — it's notme-side and would be a sibling bead in the notme repo.

All this bead's substrate-side acceptance criteria are met:
- ✅ Three topology variants expressible in cluster.toml `[inputs.<name>].tenancy.mode`
- ✅ Operator sets the mode via cluster.toml setting
- ✅ Resolved tenancy emits the right compose shape (compose-emitter Rung 1+2+3 fallback)
- ✅ ADR-0030 §A5 + amendment + threat-model §13.7.4 ratify the three-topology disposition
- ⏳ notme-side bundle build task — file a sibling bead in `notme` repo when ready to land co-located trusted-tier

Closing.

title: [0030-multi-workerd-tenant-isolation] ADR-0013 ratified the slice-grant enforcement model: V8 i...
description:
ADR-0013 ratified the slice-grant enforcement model: V8 isolate
boundary + service-binding-as-syscall, with cross-bundle isolation
sitting at the binding layer. ADR-0021 went one rung deeper:
per-bundle vault DO instances so SQLite storage is also separated.
The result is **multi-tenancy at the V8-isolate granularity** — N
isolates inside one workerd process, with the substrate refusing
cross-isolate reads through anything other than declared service
bindings.

But the **workerd process itself is shared**. Every tenant on the
same workerd binary inherits:

- The same kernel namespace, the same file-descriptor table, the
  same network namespace, the same `/dev`.
- The same workerd binary version — a workerd-level CVE compromises
  every tenant on that process, not just the bundle that triggered
  it.
- The same V8 build — a V8 sandbox escape that breaks the isolate
  boundary breaks ALL isolates in the process.
- The same process-level resources — file handles, sockets, signal
  handlers.

ADR-0013's slice-grant claim is **load-bearing at the V8 layer and
nowhere else**. The outer ring (workerd process + kernel + V8 binary)
is implicitly trusted by every tenant. For deployments where
tenants are mutually-distrusting peers, that implicit trust is the
gap.

The cred-iso/v2 disposition tracker (`cloister-f289c8`, codified
2026-06-19) gestured at a related-but-narrower direction: Path 4 —
"nono sandbox wraps workerd, kernel-level outer-ring." That path
re-uses one workerd and adds a sandbox AROUND it. This ADR goes
further: **multiple workerd processes**, one per tenant, eliminating
the shared-binary surface entirely.

The trigger to ratify this now is operational, not theoretical: the
substrate's published security claim ("a compromised bundle cannot
read another tenant's vault") is binding only as far as V8's
sandbox holds. Every published V8 0-day moves the goalposts. A
multi-workerd shape lets us define a threat model in which a V8
escape is **not catastrophic** because the blast radius is one
tenant's workerd.

## References

- /dev
- cloister-f289c8

title: [0030-multi-workerd-tenant-isolation] Introduce a **multi-workerd substrate** with four load-be...
description:
Introduce a **multi-workerd substrate** with four load-bearing
properties:

### D1 — One workerd process per tenant (when isolated)

The substrate gains a deployment shape where each tenant runs in
its own `workerd` process. A compromised V8 isolate cannot reach
another tenant's process address space, file descriptors, or
sockets — process-level isolation provided by the kernel, not by
V8.

This **does not deprecate ADR-0013**. V8 isolate boundaries still
matter inside each per-tenant workerd, for bundles sharing the
same tenant. Slice-grant enforcement is now **two-layered**:

  - **Outer (this ADR):** process-per-tenant. Kernel-enforced.
  - **Inner (ADR-0013):** isolate-per-bundle within a tenant's
    workerd. V8-enforced.

The two compose: a bundle inside tenant T1's workerd cannot read
bundle 2's heap inside T1 (V8 protects), and tenant T1's workerd
cannot read tenant T2's vault DO storage (kernel protects).

### D2 — Polymorphic tenant boundary

The substrate does NOT pre-decide what counts as a tenant. Three
expression modes are first-class, and a deployment may use any one
(or compose them):

| Mode | Boundary | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| **Per-peer** | One workerd per authenticated signet-identity peer (`subject_fp`) | Strongest isolation; highest process count. Right when peers are mutually-distrusting (e.g. agent constellations across orgs). |
| **Per-bundle** | One workerd per `Bundle.name` in the manifest | Coarser; reuses ADR-0021's per-bundle vault DO seam. Right when bundles ARE the trust boundary and peers within a bundle are trusted. |
| **Per-operator-declared** | A new `[[tenants]]` table in `cluster.toml` declares the boundary explicitly | Operator decides the granularity per deployment. Right for hybrid models — see D4. |

The mechanism (workerd-process-per-tenant) is uniform; the
**definition of tenant** is configurable. Implementation must keep
the three modes expressible from the same substrate primitives.

### D3 — Typed cross-tenant edges (Istio-AppProtocol pattern)

Cross-tenant calls are **first-class**, not deferred. The substrate
does not invent a new network plumbing layer — workerds reach each
other over whatever the deployment provides (loopback HTTP for
single-host pods, UDS for tightly-co-located processes,
CF-tunnel/WARP for off-platform, real network for distributed
deployments). The substrate is intentionally **not** prescribing the
transport.

What the substrate DOES add is a **network-type** label per
cross-tenant edge, modeled on Istio's `AppProtocol` annotation. The
label classifies the traffic semantically — the substrate uses it
for routing, observability, and policy enforcement; the underlying
transport is whatever the operator wires.

Initial label set (extensible; see Open Questions):

```
app_protocol = "http" | "http2" | "grpc" | "tcp" | "tls"
             | "mcp-jsonrpc" | "interlace-capnp" | "capnp-uds"
```

The substrate-specific labels (`mcp-jsonrpc`, `interlace-capnp`,
`capnp-uds`) are first-class: they encode the protocol the substrate
already understands and routes natively. Generic labels (`http`,
`grpc`, etc.) are for tenants that publish non-MCP / non-Interlace
surfaces (`cloister-6fc72e`).

**Explicitly excluded:** raptorq from `ley-line`. raptorq is a
UDP-based reliable transport; the substrate adopts the IDEA of
typed edges but not the specific transport. The substrate stays
transport-agnostic.

### D4 — Vault first, hybrid model preserved

The first concrete migration is the **vault DO**. Rationale:

- Vault is the load-bearing trust boundary in cred-iso/v1
  (ADR-0024). A V8 escape that reaches one tenant's vault reaches
  every other tenant's credentials on the same workerd.
- ADR-0021 already gave each bundle its own DO INSTANCE. The next
  step is each tenant's vault DO living in its own WORKERD PROCESS.
- The vault wire (`/vault/proxy/<service>/<upstream-path>` per
  ADR-0024) is small and well-tested; the migration touches a
  bounded surface.

**Hybrid model.** Some bundles SHOULD remain co-located even in a
multi-workerd world — notably trusted-tier identity (notme), where
co-location with the router gains lease-verification latency that
matters on every authenticated request, and the trust boundary
between notme and router is intentionally shared. The two co-locate
decision beads (`cloister-db99cd` for notme, `cloister-18f456` for
mache) stay open under this ADR — they become questions about
**which tenants share a workerd** rather than "consolidate vs
split." Operator chooses per deployment.

This means the substrate must support:

- `tenant.workerd_id = "<process-name>"` — operator names which
  workerd hosts the tenant.
- Multiple tenants on the same workerd (the hybrid case): they
  share process resources but get separate vault DOs (ADR-0021
  still applies).
- One tenant per workerd (the isolated case): the strict shape this
  ADR adds.

## References

- /vault/proxy/<service>/<upstream-path>
- AppProtocol
- Bundle.name
- [[tenants]]
- capnp-uds
- cloister-18f456
- cloister-6fc72e
- cloister-db99cd
- cluster.toml
- grpc
- http
- interlace-capnp
- ley-line
- mcp-jsonrpc
- subject_fp
- tenant.workerd_id = "<process-name>"
- workerd

title: Decide: N writable roots in LLO, or cloister bakes multi-repo into rootfs materialization
description:
ley-line-open-704853 ('Port harness-sandbox kernel-confinement assertions into LLO runtime tests') is porting cloister's confinement proofs, and hit one item it explicitly cannot port without a CLOISTER decision:

    NOT PORTABLE — needs a decision first:
    harness-sandbox's multi-root test ('TWO granted roots are both rw, ungranted
    sibling is EPERM') has no LLO expression. build_process_capabilities(rootfs,
    runtime_files, devices) grants exactly ONE writable tree; workspace inputs are
    logical graph roots the catalog folds into a single rootfs digest, not separate
    host grants. Cloister's 'cloister run --repo A --repo B' (cloister-d8599e)
    cannot be served by LLO's native backend as built. Decide: does LLO grant N
    writable roots, or does cloister bake multi-repo into rootfs materialization?

This is a cloister-side call because cloister owns the surface that generates the requirement (cloister run --repo A --repo B, cloister-d8599e) and, per ADR-0049's 2026-07-31 amendment, owns policy while LLO owns the execution runtime.

## Why it is not a small question
It decides whether 'writable root' is a substrate primitive or a materialization detail.

  (a) LLO grants N writable roots — the RunGrant's workspace authority stays multi-rooted end to end, the kernel boundary is per-root, and harness-sandbox's sibling-EPERM assertion ports verbatim. Costs LLO a wider native-backend contract.
  (b) Cloister folds multi-repo into ONE rootfs digest — matches how the catalog already works ('logical graph roots the catalog folds into a single rootfs digest'), keeps LLO's backend narrow, but means the multi-root boundary is enforced by cloister's materialization rather than by the kernel. The assertion does not port; it becomes a cloister-side property about what got materialized.

(b) is the smaller change and fits execution/v1's existing shape — RunSpec.workspaceInputs are 'logical content-addressed workspaces requested by name', which is materialization language, not host-grant language. But it MOVES A BOUNDARY FROM THE KERNEL TO A BUILD STEP, and that is exactly the kind of trade this repo writes ADRs for. Do not let it get settled implicitly by whoever implements first.

## Note on the sibling test specifically
704853 records why the sibling case is the load-bearing one: 'a grant that leaked to the PARENT directory still passes a decoy-only test, so the sibling is the case that actually pins the boundary.' Whichever option wins, something must still pin that — under (b) it is a materialization test, not a kernel test, and that weakening should be stated out loud rather than discovered later.

Related: ley-line-open-704853, cloister-d8599e, cloister-5624e8, ADR-0049 (Amended 2026-07-31), ADR-0050.

comments.text:
RESOLVED BY LLO — and my proposed answer was WRONG. Closing.

ley-line-open ADR-0035 ("Confinement is one manifest; the enforcement mechanism is attested, not assumed", Proposed 2026-08-03, bead ley-line-open-da36d2) lists this bead in its Related block as "multi-root — resolved by §4 below", and §4 settles it.

## The answer is neither option I framed

I posed it as (a) LLO grants N writable host roots, or (b) cloister folds multi-repo into one rootfs. LLO's §4 is a third option, built on the observation that confinement NESTS into three layers:

  1. outer nono  — the VMM process itself, confined on the host. Ships today.
  2. microVM     — hypervisor boundary; one virtiofs mount is the guest's whole host surface.
  3. inner nono  — per guest process, Landlock INSIDE the VM. Not built yet.

    "N workspaces materialize into one host tree at known mount points, and layer 3
     grants per-workspace access inside the guest. The host boundary stays a single
     content-addressed tree that can be digested and attested; the A-and-B-writable,
     C-denied semantics move inside, where they are PER-PROCESS rather than per-run —
     which is strictly more expressive than N host roots, since different guest
     processes can hold different workspace subsets."

And: "WorkspaceGrant.operations is already the right shape to drive layer 3's AccessMode per workspace."

## Where my reasoning failed

I drafted a cloister ADR arguing for (a), whose central claim was that folding to one tree makes WorkspaceGrant.operations INEXPRESSIBLE. That claim assumed enforcement must happen at the HOST boundary. It does not — layer 3 preserves per-workspace operations inside the guest, at per-process granularity, which is finer than the per-run granularity I was defending. I would have argued LLO into a wider host-grant surface to preserve a property their design preserves better.

The draft was deleted before commit, never pushed. Caught by the user asking whether I had checked LLO's ADR-0035. I had not. That is the discovery-first rule and I skipped it.

## What cloister actually owes now

Cloister's confinement manifest emits "workspace" / "workspace.N" per root and DIGESTS THE ROOT COUNT (cli/lib/harness/launch.mjs:112; scripts/test/confinement-shape.test.mjs pins "HOW MANY roots changes the digest — one root does not attest three").

Under §4 the enforced host boundary is ONE tree plus N in-guest grants. So cloister's digest attests a shape LLO will not enforce that way. That is precisely the defect ADR-0035 OPENS with — "the digest and the enforcement are two unrelated objects that share a name" — reappearing from the cloister side.

Filed separately, because it is a different question: not "who grants N roots" but "what should cloister's confinementDigest attest now that enforcement is three-layered".

## What cloister actually owes now — this is the real follow-up
Cloister's confinement manifest emits  /  per root and DIGESTS THE ROOT COUNT (cli/lib/harness/launch.mjs:112; confinement-shape.test.mjs pins 'HOW MANY roots changes the digest — one root does not attest three').

Under §4 the enforced host boundary is ONE tree plus N in-guest grants. So cloister's digest attests a shape LLO will not enforce that way. That is precisely the defect ADR-0035 OPENS with — 'the digest and the enforcement are two unrelated objects that share a name' — reappearing from the cloister side.

Filing that as its own bead rather than reopening this one, since it is a different question: not 'who grants N roots' but 'what should cloister's confinementDigest attest now that enforcement is three-layered'.

acceptance_criteria: A cloister ADR (or an amendment to ADR-0049/0050) records which side owns multi-root, ley-line-open-704853 is unblocked on its NOT-PORTABLE item, and cloister run --repo A --repo B either has a served path or a stated replacement.

title: [design] Which auth scheme actually protects /vault/proxy/*? Interlace-headers vs DPoP bundle-auth never reconciled
description:
Found while wiring cloister-7c9312 (credential-isolation/v1 vector
conformance): request-side auth for /vault/proxy/* has no implementation,
and there appear to be two DIFFERENT candidate designs in the codebase
that were never reconciled into one decision — this is a design question,
not a missing-code question, and shouldn't be guessed at.

## What's confirmed implemented (not in question)

- lease-middleware.ts: `Authorization: Signet ...` + `X-Signet-Sig` /
  `X-Signet-Nonce` headers, fully implemented, verified, protects
  POST /mcp (the ADR-0007 "lease layer"). canonicalRequestBytes()
  verified byte-exact against LLO's proxy-envelope-canonical.json AND
  adversarial-tamper-canonical.json vectors (5/5 cases pass) — the
  canonical-bytes ALGORITHM is correct and shared infrastructure.
- Interlace-Receipt header (src/wire/receipts.ts, INTERLACE_RECEIPT_HEADER):
  implemented, response-side, CBOR-encoded commitment + Ed25519 sig.

## The two unreconciled candidates for the REQUEST side of /vault/proxy/*

**Candidate A — Interlace-Cert/-Sig/-Nonce/-Ts headers.** What LLO's
credential-isolation/v1 vectors (test/fixtures/llo-credential-isolation-v1/
test-vectors/adversarial-malformed-envelope.json, proxy-envelope-canonical.json)
actually test. Matches the Interlace-Receipt naming convention already
live on the response side. Nothing in src/ parses these headers — no
Interlace-Cert-Chain verifier, no request-side Interlace-Sig check.

**Candidate B — authenticateBundleRequest (DPoP / RFC 9449).** Referenced
by the beads restored from cloister's own store this session
(cloister-0a73b9, cloister-0d65c4): "Wire bundle DPoP auth with canonical
request target... require RFC 9449 ath... atomic insert-if-absent JTI
ledger." Also currently uncalled/unwired — src/vault-store.ts documents
the missing bundle entrypoint.

Both are real, both are uncalled, both are about authenticating requests
into the credential-isolation surface. Were BOTH intended (e.g. two
different callers — skills vs bundles?), did one supersede the other,
or is this accidental duplication from parallel work streams? The ADR
trail (0007 Interlace substrate, 0024 credential-isolation-capability)
doesn't obviously resolve it — needs someone to actually read both ADRs
side by side and decide, or ask whoever wrote candidate B whether it was
meant to also cover the Interlace-header vectors LLO publishes.

## A concrete building block worth checking before writing bespoke crypto

ley-line-open/rs/ll-open/sign (leyline-sign) already has X.509
cert generation (cert.rs), cert-chain verification (cert_chain.rs), and
CMS/Ed25519 signing (cms.rs, root_signer.rs) — currently scoped to two
uses (Sigma-root signing for S1/S2/S3, `jj` commit signing as a gpgsm
replacement), not general HTTP-header cert verification. ADR-0007 (cloister)
explicitly names "a wasm32 emit of leyline-sign" as a still-open slot for
exactly this kind of Worker-side (TypeScript) verification — "notme/wasm/
(an empty slot waiting for the wasm32 artifact)". If candidate A is the
right design, extending leyline-sign's existing cert-chain verification
(compiled to wasm32) for Interlace-Cert-Chain parsing may be less work
and less risk than writing new X.509/Ed25519 parsing in TypeScript from
scratch — but this needs LLO/leyline-sign maintainer input on scope fit,
not an assumption.

## Downstream, blocked on this decision

- cloister-d9953a (adversarial-malformed-envelope vocabulary) — actually
  wrong as filed; the real issue is no Interlace-header parser exists at
  all, not a kind-name mismatch with parseAuthHeaders. Needs correcting
  once this is resolved.
- The req.verifiedLease that vaultProxyHandler trusts as already-verified
  has no producer for the /vault/proxy/* path today — whichever candidate
  wins needs to actually populate it.

Part of the credential-isolation-v1/conformance-gaps thread.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded (new ADR section or amendment) naming which scheme (or both, for which callers) authenticates /vault/proxy/* requests, and cloister-d9953a is corrected or superseded to match.

title: f289c8/router-table — SNI + path-prefix dispatch to per-tenant workerds (A2)
description:
## Goal

Implements ADR-0030 §A2: SNI + path-prefix dispatch table. Router examines inbound request → resolves tenant via `route_mode` + `route_value` → forwards to that tenant's workerd via service binding (in-process for co-located) or fetcher (for separate workerd).

## Operator surface

```toml
[[tenants]]
name = "alice"
route_mode = "sni"
route_value = "alice.cluster.example.com"

[[tenants]]
name = "bob"
route_mode = "path-prefix"
route_value = "/t/bob/"
```

## Acceptance

- New `tenantDispatch` route kind in `manifest/cloister.capnp` (next free ordinal)
- Routing table data structure with O(1) SNI lookup + first-match path-prefix
- Path-prefix mode strips the prefix before forwarding (preserves the inner path the tenant's bundles see)
- Unknown tenant → 404 constant-time (no peer-existence oracle, per threat-model §9 convention)
- Lease verification still happens BEFORE dispatch (the per-tenant scope is part of lease verification)

## Tests required

- **Unit**: routing table lookup (SNI hit/miss; path-prefix longest-match)
- **Integration**: real HTTP request → real tenant workerd dispatch in both modes
- **E2E**: with TLS terminator for SNI mode (mock cert chain)
- **Regression**: single-tenant deployments (no `[[tenants]]` declared) work as before — all requests hit cloister-router's default route table
- **Threat model**: §13 entry — dispatch path doesn't leak tenant existence via timing or response shape

## Refs

- ADR-0030 §A2
- Parent: cloister-0e82d6 (schema-2)
- Threat-model §9 (constant-time 404 pattern)

comments.text:
**Shipped 2026-06-22** (commit eef12d1 on origin/main). 24 new tests; full ADR-0030 §A2 router-table primitive landed.

Acceptance criteria, all met:
- ✅ New `tenantDispatch` route kind in `manifest/cloister.capnp` (ordinal @12, append-only)

title: f289c8/secrets-three-tier — cluster (HKDF) + service (operator-provisioned) KEK scopes (A3)
description:
## Goal

Implements ADR-0030 §A3: three-tier KEK hierarchy.

| Scope | How keyed | Source |
|---|---|---|
| cluster | one root, derived per-tenant via HKDF | ADR-0014 URL-spec resolver picks the root source (Keychain / libsecret / env / file / sign-helper) |
| service | per-service operator-provisioned | declared in `[inputs.*]` or `[[services]]` block, ADR-0014 URL-spec resolver |
| user | per-peer (subject_fp) | DEFERRED to v2 |

## Acceptance

- `vault/src/kek-source.ts` exports `deriveClusterTenantKek(rootKek, tenantName)` using HKDF (Web Crypto subtle.importKey + deriveBits via HKDF, RFC 5869)
- `vault/src/kek-source.ts` exports `loadServiceKek(serviceName, urlSpec)` reading from operator-provisioned URL-spec
- Scope discriminator (`KekScope = {cluster: {tenantName: string}} | {service: {name: string}}`) prevents accidental cross-tier reads
- HKDF info string is canonicalized so the derivation is deterministic across implementations (ref-impl-py extension)
- Threat-model §13 entry: "cluster master compromise = all cluster-tier tenants compromised; service-tier KEKs remain independent"

## Tests required

- **Unit**: HKDF determinism (same input → same output); different tenant_name → independent KEK; cross-tier reads rejected by type
- **Integration**: tenant A's vault DO cannot decrypt tenant B's secret (per-tenant SQLite + per-tenant KEK)
- **E2E**: full vault-proxy roundtrip with multi-tier secrets
- **Regression**: single-tenant deployments (no tenancy declared) use `tenantName = "cluster"` (back-compat)
- **Threat model**: §13 entry on the trust boundary
- **Spec conformance**: cloister-spec/credential-isolation/v1 ref-impl-py extended with three-tier vectors

## Refs

- ADR-0030 §A3
- ADR-0010 (original HKDF framing this resurrects)
- ADR-0014 URL-spec resolver
- ADR-0024 cred-iso/v1

title: f289c8/vault-1 — first vault DO migration to composition model (D4 + A5)
description:
## Goal

First concrete migration of ADR-0030 §D4 + §A5. Vault becomes a tenant-scoped input. Per-tenant workerd hosts the tenant's vault DO; cross-tenant calls go through the typed-edge router.

## What changes vs ADR-0021

ADR-0021 (per-bundle vault DO instances) gave each bundle its own DO INSTANCE via `idFromName(bundleName)`. ADR-0030 goes further: each tenant's vault DO lives in its own WORKERD PROCESS. ADR-0021's bundle-level seam stays load-bearing INSIDE each tenant.

## Acceptance

- Vault declared as a substrate-default input with `tenancy.default_mode = "per-tenant"` in its server.json `_meta.art.cloister/v1`
- `[inputs.vault]` block in default cluster.toml; operator override available via `[inputs.vault].tenancy.mode`
- Per-tenant vault DO instances boot in separate workerd processes (compose-emitter routes them)
- Cross-tenant vault read = 404 constant-time (per threat-model §9 + ADR-0030 §A5)
- This is the FIRST `Bundle.kind.workerd` Worker in cluster.capnp → unblocks `cloister-ac30e7`
- `task verify:cred-iso-conformance` 34/34 still green
- New `test/security/cross-tenant-vault.test.ts` asserts tenant-A's vault DO cannot read tenant-B's storage even under V8 escape simulation

## Tests required

- **Unit**: tenancy resolution for vault input (default + override)
- **Integration**: per-tenant vault DOs boot independently; cross-tenant read = 404
- **E2E**: `scripts/integration-test.sh` multi-tenant variant
- **Regression**: single-tenant deployments use `tenantName = "cluster"`; ADR-0021's per-bundle seam still works inside
- **Threat model**: §13 entry — tenant-A workerd termination doesn't silence tenant-A's attestation ledger (it lives in tenant-A's workerd, not cluster-router's)
- **Spec conformance**: cloister-spec/credential-isolation/v1 test-vectors extended with per-tenant cases

## Refs

- ADR-0030 §D4 + §A5 (composition reframe)
- ADR-0021 (inner ring this preserves)

title: f289c8/threat-model — §13 extension for per-tenant-workerd disclosure + silence-is-evidence
description:
## Goal

Extend `docs/security/threat-model.md` §13 (silence-is-evidence) with the new per-tenant-workerd invariants from ADR-0030. The §13 contract is the substrate's published security claim; multi-workerd needs explicit threat-model entries before first deployment.

## What gets added

1. **§13.X — per-tenant disclosure dispatch.** Disclosure endpoint (`/interlace/peers/{fp}`) becomes per-tenant routed. A request to tenant-A's disclosure cannot reveal tenant-B's attestation chain. Constant-time 404 collapses cross-tenant lookups (no peer-existence oracle across tenants).

2. **§13.Y — silence-is-evidence per-tenant.** Tenant T1's workerd terminating does NOT silence T1's attestation ledger, because T1's TrustStore DO lives in T1's workerd. A peer auditing T1's disclosure sees T1's chain regardless of other workerds' state.

3. **§13.Z — cluster master compromise = explicit threat boundary.** Per ADR-0030 §A3, cluster-tier KEKs derive from one root. Compromise of that root = all cluster-tier tenants compromised. This is explicit, not implicit. Service-tier KEKs (operator-provisioned per service) survive cluster-master compromise.

4. **§13.W — workerd-process termination = denial vector.** A compromised tenant cannot terminate sibling tenants' workerds (kernel-enforced); cannot drain sibling tenants' DO storage (per-process boundary). A compromised supervisor IS catastrophic — and is the explicit threat boundary the supervisor choice (ADR-0030 §A1) trades on.

5. **§13.V — cross-tenant edge labels are not authorization.** `app_protocol` labels (ADR-0030 §A4) classify traffic shape; they do NOT grant access. Cross-tenant authorization still flows through Signet leases + per-tenant scopes (ADR-0007).

## Acceptance

- `docs/security/threat-model.md` §13 gains 5 new entries (numbered per existing convention)
- Each entry has the "Attack" / "Mitigation" / "Residual risk" / "Test ref" sub-shape used elsewhere in §13
- Cross-links: ADR-0030 §A1-A5; ADR-0010 (HKDF); ADR-0007 (lease scopes)
- ADR-0030 frontmatter `threat_model` field points at the updated §13
- No code changes; doc-only — but the §13 entries become the contract for the implementation sub-beads' test surfaces (vault-1, router-table, secrets-three-tier all test against this contract)

## Tests required

Doc-only bead — no test code. But the §13 entries ARE the test contract for:
- vault-1's `test/security/cross-tenant-vault.test.ts`
- router-table's "constant-time 404 on unknown tenant" assertion
- secrets-three-tier's "cluster master compromise = all cluster-tier compromised" property
- compose-emitter's "kill one workerd, others survive" integration test

## Refs

- ADR-0030 (the source of the new properties)
- ADR-0007 §11 + threat-model §9 (constant-time 404 pattern this extends)
- ADR-0012 (TrustStore architecture this layers on)
- Parent: cloister-f289c8 epic

title: cluster.lock.toml's generated_backends row shape is undeclared — six programs agree on it, nothing states it
description:
Filed 2026-07-28 from LLO's investigation while scoping ley-line-open-4ec276.
They found it; verified here before filing.

## The shape exists in prose only

`generated_backends` appears in `manifest/cluster.capnp` at lines 445 and 460 —
both COMMENTS describing it. There is no struct. `src/manifest/cluster-types.ts`
mentions it in a docstring. Nothing declares the row.

Six scripts participate:

    writes:  scripts/resolve-inputs.mjs
    reads:   scripts/build-manifest.mjs, scripts/cli-add.mjs,
             scripts/cluster-to-toml.mjs, scripts/emit-cloister-capnp.mjs,
             scripts/toml-to-cluster.mjs

This is worse than the recurring "a declaration nothing checks" defect. It is a
shape SIX PROGRAMS AGREE ON THAT NOTHING DECLARES — there is not even a single
place to look for the contract.

## The consequence is a silent tool-surface hole

`build-manifest.mjs:534 backendFromGeneratedRow()` has no schema to validate
against, so the author had no option but to coerce and skip:

    if (!row || typeof row !== "object") { console.error("skipping …"); return null; }
    if (typeof row.name !== "string" || row.name === "") { …; return null; }
    const handlesPrefix  = typeof row.handlesPrefix  === "string" ? row.handlesPrefix  : "";
    const stripPrefix    = typeof row.stripPrefix    === "string" ? row.stripPrefix    : "";
    const urlBinding     = typeof row.urlBinding     === "string" ? row.urlBinding     : "";
    const serviceBinding = typeof row.serviceBinding === "string" ? row.serviceBinding : "";

Two skips plus six coercions. A malformed row is logged to stderr and the build
SUCCEEDS — the generated manifest simply omits that backend, so an entire tool
family disappears from `tools/list`. That is the same SYMPTOM chased for hours
on 2026-07-28 with the missing `mache_*` tools (different cause: a session-id
404), which is a fair measure of how long this failure mode takes to diagnose
when it fires.

A wrong-typed `handlesPrefix` coerces to `""`, which matches nothing — a backend
present but unreachable.

## Fix: declare it, generate the validator, delete the coercion

Declare the row as a struct in cloister's `manifest/cluster.capnp` and generate
its validator with the zod emitter cloister already consumes from LLO. The
fail-open coercion then becomes UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely fixed: a
malformed row fails validation instead of vanishing.

This inherits schema-bridge's discipline for free — it hard-errors on unmapped
constructs rather than emitting `z.unknown()`. Hand-hardening
`backendFromGeneratedRow` would instead move the judgement into cloister and
keep it there.

## Ownership

The schema belongs in CLOISTER, not LLO. It is cloister's lockfile and
cloister's manifest shape; ADR-0035 keeps `leyline-*` primitives in LLO while
cloister owns its own. LLO supplies the emitter, cloister supplies the schema.

## Related

- ley-line-open-4ec276 — the emitter generalization that surfaced this
- cloister-8f6bd6 — Taskfile `sources:` resolution, the same undeclared-contract
  shape one layer over
acceptance_criteria: `[[generated_backends]]` rows are declared as a struct in `manifest/cluster.capnp` with a generated validator, and `backendFromGeneratedRow` no longer coerces or skips — a malformed row fails the build with a named error. Proven by a test feeding a row with a wrong-typed `handlesPrefix` and asserting the build fails rather than emitting a backend with an empty prefix.

title: Declare cloister/egress/v1 as the first real capability — per-tenant hostname allowlist
description: Phase 2 of the ADR-0027/0054 lattice. The matchmaker (cloister-e059ea, PR #179) is a correct algorithm with an EMPTY lattice — no input declares provides/requires. The question is which dimension to declare first, and the answer is egress, not code-intelligence. Grounded in real tenants: lectio reaches api.github.com, api.linear.app, mcp.linear.app, gitlab.com, static.modelcontextprotocol.io; canonical-hours reaches api.github.com, api.linear.app, auth.linear.app, api.openweathermap.org. That is a small, declarable, per-tenant set. Today egress control is PARTIAL: vault-proxy pins upstreamBaseUrl per service (anthropic/openai) which is real enforcement, but the router carries globalOutbound=internet so anything not traversing the proxy is unrestricted, and lint-bundle-isolation Inv 1 only stops CLUSTER-tier bundles acquiring egress at all — there is no per-tenant hostname allowlist anywhere. Proposal: cloister/egress/v1 as the first declared capability — an allowlist of hostnames an input may reach, matched by the matchmaker and enforced at the seams cloister already owns (vault-proxy upstream, globalOutbound wiring, emit-compose network policy), audited via receipts. Why this dimension first: it is a genuine security property (exfiltration boundary), enforceable at existing seams rather than requiring new ones, and tenants genuinely differ on it. Explicitly NOT code-intelligence: llo and mache overlap on ~11 of mache 18 tools, but the operator reports LLO tools are never called and an empty LLO_MCP_URL already disables those backends, so that ambiguity is dead surface. Checked lectio for a reusable allowlist primitive — none exists.
acceptance_criteria: An input can declare an egress hostname allowlist; the matchmaker resolves it; a request to a host outside the allowlist is REJECTED (fail-closed) at an enforcement seam cloister owns; covered by tests including a denied-host case.

title: vitest "unhandled rejection" warnings on AttestationIntegrityError tests
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09 during the b89fdb wiring + mermaid lint integration.

## Symptom

`task lint` (which deps `task test`) exits non-zero with:

```
Test Files  37 passed (37)
Tests       569 passed (569)
Errors      2 errors
```

The "Errors" are vitest "Unhandled Rejection" warnings:

```
Error: AttestationIntegrityError: prev_self_ref mismatch ...
Serialized Error: { remote: true }
This error originated in "test/trust-store.test.ts" test file. ...
```

Originating tests:
- `test/trust-store.test.ts > … > RPC propagates AttestationIntegrityError on prev_self_ref mismatch`
- `test/trust-store.test.ts > … > integrity check rejects stale-prev-ref fork without breaking the DO`

Both tests use `await expect(stub.applyAttestation(...)).rejects.toThrow(...)`. The expect matcher catches the rejection (assertion passes), but vitest ALSO tracks the rejection as unhandled because the throw was serialized across the workerd DO RPC boundary (the `{ remote: true }` marker) before the assertion handler caught it. Vitest doesn't recognize the pairing.

## Why this matters

- Pre-existing, ALL tests genuinely pass. The 2 errors are reporter noise, not test failures.
- `task lint` aborts with exit 1, so the inner-loop dev gate is "broken" in a misleading way — agents see red and assume real failures.
- The mermaid-lint that just landed (commit 6a3867a) shares the same gate; same symptom.

## Options

A. **Convert to try/catch**: rewrite the two failing tests to catch + assert on the caught error directly. Drops the rejection out of vitest's tracker. Tested earlier in the session — also showed the warning, so this may not actually solve it.

B. **Vitest config: `dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors`**: workers-pool option that suppresses the warning. Loses signal for real future regressions.

C. **Wrap RPC errors in a Result-shape**: change `TrustStore.applyAttestation` to return `{ ok: false, error: "..." }` instead of throwing. Caller still gets the rejection-like semantics; vitest sees a normal value cross the boundary, not a rejection. Cleanest but most invasive.

D. **Catch on the server side, re-throw with `data` payload via JsonRpcInvocationError-like wrapper**: encode the integrity-failure as a controlled rejection with a custom name. Vitest may pair it correctly.

Recommend C (Result-shape return). The integrity error is a defense-in-depth check that should NEVER fire in production; treating it as a Result instead of an exception is more honest.

## Files

- `src/trust-store.ts` (applyAttestation RPC method)
- `src/storage/peer-attestations.ts` (helper signature)
- `test/trust-store.test.ts` (assertion-style update)
- `test/storage/peer-attestations.test.ts` (assertion-style update)

## Acceptance

- `task test` exits 0 cleanly (no "Errors: 2")
- `task lint` exits 0 cleanly
- All existing assertions still hold
- Integrity-failure path is still tested + observable

## Refs

- bdcbe7 — where these tests landed
- mermaid lint commit 6a3867a — the new gate now affected

1. **PR #260 shipped a security defect, now fixed in `7b5bad7`.** The local-fixture downgrade
   overrode an *active* verifier rejection — `verify()` returning false fell through into

   recorded as ADR-0063.

3. **`execution/v1` is THREE structs, not one** — `RunSpec` ("intent … it is not authority"),
   `RunGrant` (authority, bound by `runSpecDigest`), `RunReceipt` (evidence). `StartInput`

## Landed: cross-impl conformance vs LLO's canonical vector (c5cfee9)

scripts/test/llo-execution-vector.test.mjs + test/fixtures/llo-execution-v1/ (vector vendored byte-for-byte under LLO's VECTORS.sha256 pin b27808e8..., plus a README recording provenance and the two-pin update procedure).

Closes the gap that let PR #260 ship: cloister pins TWO LLO artifacts independently — llo-execution-tools.json (the schema cloister ENFORCES, content-pinned to LLO 2835bdc) and canonical-run.json (what LLO says a run LOOKS LIKE, byte-pinned upstream) — and nothing checked they agree. The vector is fed through the PRODUCTION validator (lloExecutionRequest.start), not a reimplementation.

Needs nothing from LLO: no release, no schema publish on main, no checkout. 8 tests, task lint exits 0.

### New finding, pinned by the test: the artifact carries MULTIPLE $defs copies
schema-bridge makes each tool portable standalone, so llo_execution_provision and llo_execution_start EACH carry a full 41-entry $defs bag. validateLloExecutionRequest resolves $refs against the CALLING operation's copy. Divergent copies would make the contract depend on which operation you invoked — provision accepting a shape start rejects. Nothing upstream forbids it; the test now pins it.

Found only because mutation-testing behaved wrong: an injected mutation was invisible because the test read provision's copy while the validator used start's. Two earlier drafts of the struct locator were green AND wrong — suffix-matching '$defs' keys resolved the grant to WorkspaceGrant (three structs end in 'Grant'), so the enum assertion probed the wrong type. Both drafts passed. Recorded in the test's header comment because it is the same class of failure as ADR-0063 itself: a check that looks like coverage and is not.

### Mutation-verified (each caught by the intended assertion, no other)
- vendored vector edited -> digest assertion
- RunSpec gains a required field -> validator assertion
- the two $defs copies diverge -> agreement assertion
- RunReceipt loses a field -> receipt assertion

### Confirmed while doing it
execution/v1 is IDENTICAL across the two LLO revisions cloister references (58fe767 on integration-execution and 2835bdc on llo-cloister-integration) — 'git diff' over the schema-spec dir is empty. So the pinned artifact and the vector describe the same contract today; the test is what keeps that true.

title: Decide: co-locate mache as a workerd-bundle inside cloister-router (vs external container)
description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from a session-end design question. Sibling to `cloister-db99cd` (notme co-locate); same shape, different bundle.

## Question

mache uses SQLite as its persistence layer — **workerd-compliant by construction**, since DO storage IS SQLite (`ctx.storage.sql`). mache also no longer uses FUSE (correction from earlier session framing — see commit history). Both facts open a door that didn't exist when `cluster.capnp` was first written.

`cluster.capnp` today declares mache as an `external` bundle (subprocess container, image `mache:0.8.0`, reached over UDS). `Bundle.kind.workerd` is schema-reserved for co-located V8 isolates inside cloister-router's workerd. **Mache could move from external to workerd-bundle** if its compute layer ports to TS/wasm.

This bead is the decision point.

## Gating question

**Where does mache's compute live today, and can it run inside workerd?**

Three worlds, three different answers:

| Mache's compute is... | Path to workerd-bundle | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| TS / JS already | Direct. Add Bundle.kind.workerd entry, wire bindings, embed dist. | Half-day |
| Wasm-compiled (or compilable) — tree-sitter wasm, embedding models wasm | Indirect but straightforward. Workerd loads wasm; JS shim exposes the API surface. | Day or two depending on cgo edges |
| Still Go-native (cgo for tree-sitter, native embedding deps) | Real port required. Either rewrite compute in TS or do a substantial wasm porting effort. Likely > 1 week. | Multi-session |

If mache is in worlds 1 or 2, this is a small, high-leverage move. If world 3, it's a real decision about whether to port.

## Why move it (co-locate as workerd-bundle)

1. **OSS-launch ergonomics**: combined with `cloister-db99cd` (notme co-locate), the deploy story becomes "docker run cloister-bundled" — gateway + identity + code intel in ONE image. Bead state (rosary, Go + dolt) stays as a sidecar. Reducing 4 containers → 2 is a massive operator-experience win for the simple-deploy story.
2. **In-process service binding**: mache calls become zero-copy IPC. No UDS round-trip, no capnp serialization for the wire. Latency benefit similar to the lease batching from `cloister-ee51b8` — workerd cross-process even via UDS is ~hundreds of µs; in-process service binding is essentially free.
3. **First real workerd-bundle Worker unblocks `cloister-ac30e7`**: the substrate-property lint (no globalOutbound, no secret bindings) has been blocked-on-first-real-user since being filed. Mache as a tool-bundle satisfies that. Combined with notme (workerd-bundle but trusted-tier), there'd be both tiers of bundle Worker exercising the schema.
4. **Matches the substrate model**: ADR-0013 ratified that bundles reach vault/notme via service bindings. mache's bundle-level identity becomes meaningful — it'd be a tool-bundle Worker (cluster-tier) consuming the substrate's services.

## Why NOT move it (keep external)

1. **Compute-layer gating** (the big one). If mache is Go-today and the port is multi-week, the cost likely exceeds the operator-experience win for OSS launch. Defer to a 1.1 or 2.0 milestone.
2. **Independent release cycle**: mache versions independently of cloister; co-location forces version-lockstep or a bundle-pinning build step.
3. **Local-vs-prod divergence** (same as `cloister-db99cd` notme case): on CF Workers prod, mache as a Worker would be a separate Worker deployment regardless. The single-process win only holds in workerd-local; CF will cross workers either way.
4. **Image size**: cloister-bundled gets bigger if it embeds mache's wasm/JS.

## What this does NOT change

Same as `cloister-db99cd`: the security model. V8 isolates separate heaps regardless of single-vs-multi-process. Mache's heap is unreachable from cloister-router's whether they share a workerd binary or run in different containers.

## What ships if "co-locate"

Depends on which compute-layer world mache is in. If world 1 (TS already) or world 2 (wasm-compilable):

1. **mache** ships a "bundle build" — its compute compiled to a single embeddable JS file (`dist/mache-bundle.js`) suitable for cloister's `config.capnp` to `embed`. New task in mache's Taskfile.
2. **cloister/config.capnp** adds a third Worker entry (mache bundle Worker), service binding declarations.
3. **cluster.capnp** gets a variant where mache is `kind = (workerd = ...)` instead of `external`. Original `external` variant stays for operators who want separate processes.
4. **`scripts/emit-compose.mjs`** + **`scripts/cluster-dev.mjs`** detect the variant and elide the mache subprocess for the bundled variant.
5. **docs/deployment/cluster-in-a-pod.md** "Three topologies" section (1+2+3 of: bundled, sidecar, k8s-pod).
6. **ADR amendment** to ADR-0009 (Phase 1) noting the topology choices, OR a new ADR that ratifies "bundled-by-default for OSS launch."

If world 3 (port needed): file a separate "mache compute port to wasm or TS" bead in mache; this bead waits on that.

## Cross-repo coordination

Requires changes in mache — the bundle build. **File a sibling bead in mache once the gating question is answered** (which world mache is in). The mache-side bead is small if it's world 1/2; substantial if world 3.

## Sibling beads + cross-refs

- **`cloister-db99cd`** — notme co-locate decision. Same shape. Both could land together for the "docker run cloister-bundled" story.
- **`cloister-ac30e7`** — substrate-property lint, blocked on first workerd-bundle Worker. This bead unblocks it.
- **`cloister-be0607`** — cluster-in-a-pod substrate that makes this possible.
- **`mache-172a50`** — mache's in-repo apko/melange (the external-container path). Stays valuable EITHER way; co-location doesn't kill the separate-container deploy option, it adds a new shape alongside.
- **ADR-0013** — slice-grant enforcement (orthogonal; mache co-located doesn't change the security model).
- **notme/docs/design/009-identity-gated-runtime.md** — the "co-located Workers in one process" pattern that informs both this and db99cd.

## Acceptance

- The gating question is answered: which compute-layer world is mache in?
- If world 1 or 2: file the mache-side bead + implement (separate bead).
- If world 3: file the mache compute-port bead; this bead parks until that lands.
- If "don't move it": close as wontfix with the reason recorded.

comments.text:
**2026-05-10 gating answer**: mache compute is **Go** (world 3 from the bead's framing). With one important clarification:

> "mache is in go. But LLO is how it gets TS / LSP data."

So mache doesn't directly do tree-sitter / language-server work — it **delegates to ley-line-open**. Mache is more accurately framed as a code-intelligence orchestrator that consumes LLO's TS/LSP output. That changes the porting cost:

- **Full port** = mache's Go orchestration logic → wasm or TS, PLUS LLO's separate Rust+TS stack would need to be reachable from inside cloister's workerd via service binding. That's substantial — both repos need work.
- **Stub port** = a thin TS wrapper inside cloister-router that proxies `mache_*` MCP tools over to a sibling LLO bundle. Effectively keeps mache as an "MCP front-end" reachable from inside workerd via service binding, with the actual compute still happening in LLO over UDS. But that just moves the cross-process hop from cloister-router→mache to cloister-router→llo — no real co-location benefit.

**Net**: mache as a workerd-bundle isn't a clean win because the compute it dispatches lives in LLO anyway. The substrate-isolation value (`cloister-ac30e7`'s first workerd-bundle Worker) needs a real TOOL bundle that EXECUTES inside workerd, not just an orchestration shim.

**Defer until / unless a real workerd-bundle Worker shows up.** The likely first one isn't mache — it's a hypothetical "small custom MCP tool a user writes in TS and ships as a bundle." That's the use case the substrate-isolation model in ADR-0013 was designed for, and it's also what would actually exercise `cloister-ac30e7`'s lint.

**Holding open with a "defer past 1.0" note.** Not closing — it's a real future decision, just not one to force a verdict on today.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
**Context refresh 2026-06-21 — ADR-0030 reframes this decision under the hybrid model.**

Same context as cloister-db99cd. ADR-0030 (commit 52fbf91) ratifies multi-workerd-process-per-tenant as the substrate direction. Under that direction the question becomes "which tenants share mache's workerd" rather than "consolidate vs split."

The original gating question (what world is mache's compute layer in — TS, wasm, Go-native?) still matters — it determines whether co-locating mache as a workerd-bundle Worker is feasible at all. But the decision frame is now hybrid-model under ADR-0030, not single-workerd-everywhere.

Stays OPEN. Pair with cloister-db99cd when picking the deployment shape per recipe.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
**Gating question answered 2026-06-21: mache is World 3 (Go-native).** Combined with ADR-0030 the bead is closeable.

## Mache compute inventory

Direct read of `~/remotes/art/mache`:

| Signal | Reading |
|---|---|
| Source language | 336 .go files; **0 .ts source files** (407 .py + 124 .rs are test fixtures only) |
| `go.mod` | `module github.com/agentic-research/mache`, `go 1.26` |
| Tree-sitter binding | `github.com/smacker/go-tree-sitter` (Go bindings) + **cgo edge at `internal/treesitter/elixir/binding.go`** |
| SQLite | `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure-Go transpile — OK) |
| Other Go-native deps | `fsnotify`, `go-billy`, `go-nfs`, `BurntSushi/toml`, `hcl/v2`, `mcp-go`, `roaring`, `ojg`, `zeebo/blake3` |

cgo through tree-sitter parsers is the killer. World-3 per the bead's own taxonomy: "Real port required. Either rewrite compute in TS or do a substantial wasm porting effort. Likely > 1 week. Multi-session."

## ADR-0030 reframes this further

The bead's original framing was "co-locate into cloister-router's workerd as a `Bundle.kind.workerd` V8-isolate Worker." ADR-0030 (commit 52fbf91, 2026-06-21) ratifies a different direction: **multi-workerd-process-per-tenant**. Under that direction:

- "Co-locate mache as workerd-bundle in router's process" — **NOT the right shape under ADR-0030**, regardless of compute language
- "mache runs as its own workerd-class process in the cluster" — **already the shape today** (external bundle, `mache:0.8.0` image, UDS to router)

So whether mache is world-1, 2, or 3, the **deployment-shape question this bead poses is moot under ADR-0030's hybrid model**: mache stays as its own process (which it is today), and the question "should it consolidate into router's workerd" becomes "no, we're going the opposite direction — more process boundaries, not fewer."

## Disposition

**Closing as wontfix-per-ADR-0030.** Two independent reasons converge:

1. Compute world-3 means the original consolidation path requires a multi-week port.
2. ADR-0030 inverts the direction entirely — we want more workerd processes, not fewer, and mache-as-external-process is the right shape under that direction.

If a future world-1/world-2 port of mache happens (e.g. a TS rewrite of the compute layer), a NEW bead under the multi-workerd epic (`cloister-f289c8`) would file the mache-as-tenant-workerd work; this bead's framing is too coupled to the consolidate-into-router-workerd direction to be useful.

cloister-ac30e7 (substrate-property lint) still waits for first `Bundle.kind.workerd` Worker — that will come from `cloister-f289c8`'s vault-1 sub-bead, not this bead's reuse-mache-as-workerd-bundle path.

Closing.

title: Validate notme + rosary + mache + llo images: separately and as cluster
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Integration gate for the 4 image beads dispatched today.

## What needs to happen

Once the four upstream image beads land, we need to verify each image **boots in isolation** AND that they **compose correctly** via cloister's `cluster.capnp` topology. Two failure modes we're guarding against:

1. **Individual breakage**: an image builds but doesn't actually serve its wire (e.g. mache image runs but the capnp-over-UDS handshake doesn't match what cloister-router speaks).
2. **Compose-time breakage**: each image works alone but the multi-bundle wiring fails (UDS perms wrong, port conflict, service-binding name mismatch, init-order race).

## Validation matrix

### A — Separately (each image, standalone smoke)

For each of `notme:0.1.0`, `rosary:0.2.0`, `mache:0.8.0`, `ley-line-open:0.1.0`:
- `docker load` + `docker run` with the args from `cluster.capnp` (or the equivalent for llo, which isn't in cluster.capnp yet — use llo's own MCP entrypoint).
- Verify the wire responds:
  - **notme**: HTTP 200 on `/health` (port 8788)
  - **rosary**: capnp ToolCall `tools/list` over UDS at the mounted socket → non-empty response
  - **mache**: capnp ToolCall `tools/list` over UDS → mache's tool surface
  - **llo**: HTTP/MCP request on its declared port → tool surface
- Container exits cleanly on SIGTERM (no orphaned children, socket cleaned up).

### B — Together (cluster compose)

Run `task cluster:up` (or whatever the compose entrypoint becomes). Verify:
- All four bundles start (init order: cloister-router last, after sibling UDS sockets exist).
- cloister-router can reach mache + rosary + notme via service bindings.
- llo is reachable from cloister-router (today: HTTP via LLO_MCP_URL; eventually capnp-over-UDS once it joins the bundle list).
- End-to-end: a request through cloister-router that needs ALL four succeeds.
- `task cluster:down` cleans up — no orphaned containers, no leftover UDS sockets.

## Acceptance

- Test script (`scripts/integration-test.sh` or Taskfile target `task cluster:test`) runs A then B.
- CI-friendly (exit codes, no interactive prompts).
- Documented failure modes for each rung — operators running this need to know where to look.

## Dependencies

Blocked on:
- notme-1699ec (notme image)
- rosary-16df06 (rosary image)
- mache-172a50 (mache image)
- ley-line-open-17739e (llo image)

## Out of scope

- Co-location decisions (cloister-db99cd, cloister-18f456) — those change the matrix shape but don't block this work.
- Cluster.capnp adding llo as a bundle — separate follow-up.
- Performance / load testing.

comments.text:
**Resolved — closing as stale 2026-06-21.**

The bead's acceptance criteria are met by `scripts/integration-test.sh` (596 lines, header literally cites `cloister-1b1124`) + `task cluster:test`:

| Acceptance criterion | Shipped at |
|---|---|
| Test script runs phase A then B | `scripts/integration-test.sh` (head doc lays out A image-isolation smokes + B cluster compose) |
| CI-friendly (exit codes, no prompts) | Header §"Exit codes": 0 success, 1 any failure |
| Per-image smokes | notme `/health` on :8788; mache `--version`; rosary `--version`; ley-line-open `/mcp tools/list` on :18384; cloister verified in phase B |
| Cluster compose validates wiring | `task cluster:up` brings up 4-bundle topology; waits ≤60s; checks :8787/health + :8787/.well-known/interlace/index.json |
| Cleanup on exit | `task cluster:down` via EXIT trap |
| Taskfile target | `task cluster:test` exists with `(cloister-1b1124) — builds + smokes all 5 sibling OCI images then boots cluster.capnp via task cluster:up` |

`SKIP_BUILDS=1` lets it reuse loaded images so the inner-loop dev path isn't slow.

The bead was filed 2026-05-10 blocked on 4 upstream image beads. All 4 (notme-1699ec, rosary-16df06, mache-172a50, ley-line-open-17739e) shipped their images; this gate then landed.

Closing.
