title: ADR-0011: hypervisor vs bundle boundary + per-folder READMEs (manifest/wire/src)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09 from the user's question "what's the diff between hypervisor-level and bundle-level code? Is this 1:1 with k8s or not?"

## Two artifacts

### ADR-0011 — Hypervisor vs bundle responsibilities

Formalizes:
- Three-criterion test for "hypervisor-layer": (a) mediates between bundles or to outside, (b) compromise affects multiple bundles, (c) singleton per cluster.
- Three-criterion test for "bundle-layer": (a) scoped to one capability slice, (b) compromise = one slice's blast radius, (c) potentially many per cluster.
- External-services category (rosary/mache/LLO/signet) — neither hypervisor nor bundle; reached via `httpForward` or `leylineNet`.
- Comparison to Kubernetes:
  - 11 k8s primitives where the analogy holds (ConfigMap=cloister.capnp, Service=EdgeRoute, ...).
  - 9 k8s features where it breaks down (no pods, no scheduling, no LoadBalancer-as-primitive, no etcd, no daemonsets).
- The "80% of k8s without networking" heuristic captured precisely: cloister covers the declarative + capability-shaped 80%; the host platform fills the infrastructure-shaped 20%.

### Three new folder READMEs

- `manifest/README.md` — schema home; explains the source-of-truth flow (`<repo>/cloister.capnp` → `task manifest` → `src/generated/manifest.ts` → runtime), schema-evolution rules cite, when-to-edit checklist.
- `wire/README.md` — capnp wire schemas; documents that the Manifest codec is dead in cloister production (per ADR-0005 amendment) but kept as the publicly-shared schema for companion↔backend; includes the "why hand-rolled codec" rationale.
- `src/README.md` — layout map of the cloister-router bundle's source. ASCII tree + mermaid two-layer dispatch diagram + "where to make changes" table.

## Cross-references

- README.md doc map updated with all four new entries (ADR-0011 + 3 folder READMEs).
- ARCHITECTURE.md ADR list extended with ADR-0011.

## Verification
- task lint passes (17 test files / 235 tests).
- No code changes — pure docs.

## Out of scope
- Updating CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md to reference ADR-0011 (will fold in next sweep if the boundary criteria need to be in agent-loaded memory).
- New folder READMEs for `scripts/`, `test/`, `_agent_log/` — file headers cover the first two; `_agent_log/` should likely be gitignored or moved to `.beads/` adjacent.

## Files
- `docs/adr/0011-hypervisor-bundle-boundary.md`
- `manifest/README.md`
- `wire/README.md`
- `src/README.md`
- `README.md` (doc map)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (ADR list)

title: docs/cross-repo-audit.md is stale and states it is not
description:
Filed 2026-05-18, header still reads: 'Findings + recommended actions; no work has been done against any of the items here yet.' That is false for at least two of five, verified 2026-08-03:

- Finding #2 'rs/crates/sign/ trust-root crate duplicated across cloister/signet/ley-line/LLO' — RESOLVED. cloister's rs/crates/ now holds only cas + host-runtime. The sign crate lifted to LLO per ADR-0045.
- Finding #5 'schema-bridge tool, cloister owner + notme lifted copy' — RESOLVED. Cloister no longer vendors it; schema-bridge plugins are fetched as digest-pinned published binaries (schema-bridge.lock.json, cloister-9170d0). Only rs/target/schema-bridge remains, which is the fetch cache.

Findings #1 (capability identifier scheme) and #3/#4 need re-checking; ADR-0028 exists now, which #1 asked for.

Why this matters more than ordinary doc rot: the doc's stated purpose is 'to be the source-of-truth for what needs cross-repo coordination so future evolve cycles can reference this instead of re-discovering the same overlaps.' A stale audit that claims nothing has been done makes a future session re-investigate resolved items — the exact cost the doc exists to prevent. It is an invariant stated in prose with no rail, which is the pattern CLAUDE.md already names.

Consider whether the per-finding status belongs in the tracking beads (which git can date) rather than restated in the doc — same argument as docs/adr/INDEX.md being generated.

comments.text:
THIRD finding also resolved — verified 2026-08-03.

Finding #3 'vault/ substrate duplication, cloister + notme; notme/vault is legacy, delete on schedule (notme-9af5dd)' — RESOLVED. notme commit 0d3ec86 '[notme-9af5dd] chore(vault): retire notme/vault'. `git ls-files vault/` in notme returns nothing; only an orphaned node_modules/ remains on disk. Cloister is now the sole vault implementation (src/routes/vault-proxy.ts + vault-store.ts + the credential-store pair).

So THREE of the five findings are resolved (#2 sign crate, #3 notme/vault, #5 schema-bridge) while the header still reads 'no work has been done against any of the items here yet.' The doc is not merely stale — it understates real convergence, which makes the ecosystem look more duplicated than it is. That is the opposite of the error a stale doc usually makes and it is worth saying in the rewrite.

Also relevant to #1 (capability identifier scheme): ADR-0028 exists now, which is what the finding asked for. Needs a status check rather than a re-investigation.

Only #4 (interlace-spec consumer fanout) looks genuinely open, and it now has a bead: cloister-9d0960 covers the citation-rail half of it.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
CORRECTION to my previous comment — framing was wrong, facts stand.

notme/vault was not 'legacy code deleted on schedule.' It was **LIFTED to cloister**, and the lift is now complete on both ends:
  - cloister-9ad9eb (closed) — 'Lift notme/vault -> cloister/vault (copy-not-move; notme keeps its copy for now)'
  - notme 0d3ec86 [notme-9af5dd] 'chore(vault): retire notme/vault' — the deferred second half, now done

So the sequence was: copy into cloister, run both, then retire notme's copy. A deliberate two-phase migration that finished, not a cleanup of dead code. Cloister is the single vault implementation by design, and it got there the careful way.

This matters for how the rewrite of docs/cross-repo-audit.md should read. The audit framed #3 as 'duplication to be cleaned up.' It was actually 'migration in flight, second phase intentionally deferred.' A reader who takes the audit at face value would conclude the ecosystem was sloppy where it was in fact being deliberate — the same misreading risk as the header claiming no work has been done.

title: A new scripts/test/*.test.mjs file silently does not run — the test list is hand-maintained
description:
Found while landing cloister-71a9f4.

`task test:lint-scripts` (Taskfile.yml:1166) enumerates its 31 test files as an explicit space-separated string rather than a glob. A new file under `scripts/test/` therefore runs only if someone remembers to append it — and if they forget, the gate still exits 0 and reports a healthy test count.

This is the same defect class the row-shape bug was: a declaration nothing checks. Here the undeclared thing is a *test*, which makes it worse than average — the failure mode is a rail that exists, passes review, and never executes. The repo's own principle ("an invariant with no rail is a comment") applies to the rail's registration too.

Concretely: `scripts/test/build-manifest-row-shape.test.mjs` was written, passed locally under `node --test`, and would not have run in CI until it was hand-added to line 1166.

Two candidate fixes:

1. **Glob the directory** — `node --import tsx --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs` plus the two `tools/harness-sandbox/test/` files. Simple; the risk is a stray/WIP file entering the gate unintentionally.
2. **Keep the list, add a rail** — a test asserting that every `scripts/test/*.test.mjs` on disk appears in the Taskfile string, with an explicit opt-out marker for anything deliberately excluded. Matches the existing `lint-allow-*` convention and keeps exclusions greppable and reasoned.

(2) is more in keeping with the tree's conventions and makes the exclusion set explicit rather than implicit. (1) is less machinery but converts "forgot to add" into "forgot to exclude", which is the safer default direction.

Worth checking whether any file currently on disk is already missing from the list — that would mean a test has been silently dark for some time.
acceptance_criteria: A test file dropped into scripts/test/ either runs automatically or fails a rail naming it as unregistered. Verified by: create a deliberately-failing test file under scripts/test/, run `task lint`, and confirm the gate exits non-zero (rather than passing while ignoring it). Also audit the current list against `ls scripts/test/*.test.mjs` and report any file already missing.

title: Amend ADR-0057: parity should be generated, not asserted — declarations that cannot disagree
description:
Filed 2026-07-27 after reading vigil-4b304d. ADR-0057 (merged in #195) has a
gap that its sibling design already closes.

## What ADR-0057 says today

Declarations are authored once and settled downstream; an ACL naming a tool
that does not exist, or granting reach nothing provides, FAILS THE BUILD. That
is declare-and-check: two artifacts exist, and a gate asserts they agree.

## What vigil-4b304d asks for instead

"surface parity falling out as a GENERATED REPORT rather than an ASSERTED DIFF."

That is strictly stronger. If both sides are emitted from one source, disagreement
is not caught — it is unrepresentable. The check does not pass; it ceases to
exist.

## The evidence that the stronger form is right

vigil-4b304d's comment records the cost of the weaker one in production:
notme's `packages/contract` maintains a cross-repo byte-diff'd mirror in
notme.bot PURELY because the two halves live in different repos. That diff is
pure overhead created by the declare-and-check shape. Generate both halves from
one source and the check deletes itself.

The same bead opens with the failure mode this prevents: rosary's permission
rail asserted on a prompt STRING and stayed green while agents were instructed
to call ungranted tools. An asserted diff can check the wrong artifact and pass.
A generated pair cannot.

## Why cloister owns this

vigil-4b304d's comment names cloister as "an interception point in the CALL
path" (contrasted with signet in the RELEASE path). Cloister is where a tool
grant is checkable against an actual invocation rather than against a
description of one — `McpEdgeRoute.handlePost` -> lease verify -> `callTool`.
So ADR-0057's per-tool ACL is the surface where generated-vs-asserted has teeth.

## Scope

Amend ADR-0057 with a section distinguishing declare-and-check from
declare-and-generate, stating which surfaces warrant which, and recording that
the per-tool ACL should be generated once ley-line-open-4ec276's core exists.
Do NOT rewrite the existing decision — this is an amendment, and ADR-0057's own
model says intent is settled, never re-authored.

## Related

- vigil-4b304d — the declare-vs-generate boundary (the generation half of this
  same model; ADR-0057 is the declaration half)
- ley-line-open-4ec276 — the generator/evaluator core that makes the stronger
  form implementable; its acceptance criteria already asks for a cloister
  adoption bead
- cloister-742e19 — harness profiles, ADR-0057's motivating bead
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0057 carries an amendment section distinguishing declare-and-check from declare-and-generate, naming which of its four surfaces warrant each, and stating the condition under which the per-tool ACL moves to generated. The amendment is additive — the original decision text is unchanged.

title: Adopt LLO's generated schema surface — stop hand-mirroring credential-isolation/v1 in TS
description:
Filed 2026-07-27. This is the cloister adoption bead that
ley-line-open-4ec276's acceptance criteria explicitly asks for ("identifies
bounded implementation beads here plus adoption beads in rosary, cloister, and
vigil").

## The drift, concretely

`cloister/src/routes/vault-proxy.ts:21` hand-writes `InjectionStrategy` as a
discriminated union. It is a MIRROR of a wire spec that lives in ley-line-open:

    ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/schema-spec/credential-isolation/v1/wire/injection-strategies.md

Nothing keeps the mirror in sync. The contract is versioned precisely so it can
evolve, and a hand-copy diverges silently when it does. LLO already ships a
Python reference implementation of the same spec
(`ref-impl-py/credisolation/`), so cloister's TS is the odd one out.

Compounding it: the citing comments point at a root (`leyline-schema-spec/...`)
that resolves nowhere — see cloister-e83a33.

## Why this is smaller than it looks

Cloister does NOT vendor a schema-bridge. `rs/crates/` holds exactly two crates
(`cas`, `host-runtime`); every `schema-bridge` path under cloister is a build
artifact of LLO's crate:

    rs/target/release/capnpc-schema-bridge-zod
    rs/target/release/capnpc-schema-bridge-go

and the Taskfile already runs `cluster:zod` / `cluster:zod:verify` off that zod
plugin. The generator -> zod path from LLO into cloister is wired and running
today. Adoption widens what an existing mechanism covers; it does not introduce
a new one.

## Scope

Replace the hand-written `InjectionStrategy` union with types generated from
(or imported from) LLO's schema surface, extending the existing `cluster:zod`
pipeline rather than adding a parallel one. Delete the mirror. Fix or remove the
now-redundant path citations.

## Ordering

Blocked on ley-line-open-4ec276 landing a core that emits TS, and on
ley-line-open-4392a2 (the Apache/AGPL carveout is currently prose-only, with no
`license` field in any Cargo.toml and nothing enforcing dependency direction —
which starts mattering the moment cloister consumes generated artifacts whose
license provenance is asserted rather than declared).

Also note ley-line-open-e7f466 proposes TS bindings independently; one of the
two should own TS emission, not both.
acceptance_criteria: `src/routes/vault-proxy.ts` no longer declares `InjectionStrategy` by hand; the type comes from LLO's generated/published schema surface, wired through the existing `cluster:zod` pipeline. A test proves the consumed type matches the spec's declared variants, and `task lint` passes with no hand-mirrored copy remaining.

title: Land UDS as an input transport (ADR-0051) and unstale [inputs.llo] — else 6569de serves a socket nothing dials
description:
Filed 2026-07-28. LLO flagged this back at cloister when shipping
ley-line-open-6569de (`--mcp-uds`), and both claims verify.

## Verified

1. **`[inputs.llo]` is three releases stale.**

       [inputs.llo]
       ref = "github://.../ley-line-open/server.json@f62a5430..."
       version = "0.8.0"

   LLO's latest release is v0.11.2. So cloister is pinned to a document that
   predates `--mcp-uds`, the descriptor emitter (4ec276), the tagless OCI
   identifier (04300f), and the `remotes` -> `packages[].transport` move that
   already caused one live regression here (#210).

2. **ADR-0051 (same-host UDS as an input transport) is `status: Proposed
   (2026-07-20)`.** `uds` appears ten times in `manifest/cluster.capnp` and
   every one is `[[wires]] transport = "uds"` — bundle-to-bundle. There is NO
   UDS field on `InputSpec`. An input cannot declare a socket.

## Why this is cloister's problem, not LLO's

LLO's framing is exact: serving a socket nothing can dial is the same
write-only shape cloister has been finding all week. 6569de's acceptance
criteria — "cloister's `task smoke` can reach the daemon through notme-proxy
without `--mcp-no-auth`" — cannot be met by LLO alone. It needs an input that
can name a socket.

This is the mirror image of what cloister told LLO about `notme-proxy` being
declared but unrouted. Same defect, opposite direction, and worth noting that
each repo spotted it in the other's tree rather than its own.

## Scope

1. Bump `[inputs.llo]` to the current release, re-resolving the lockfile. Note
   this pulls in 04300f's tagless identifier — do NOT weaken cloister's digest
   pinning to accommodate it (operator direction 2026-07-28); LLO is fixing the
   image reference in 11.3. Prefer failing closed on an unpinnable reference.
2. Move ADR-0051 from Proposed to Accepted and implement: a UDS field on
   `InputSpec`, resolved into the generated backend so `LLO_MCP_URL` can name a
   socket rather than a loopback TCP port.
3. Then cloister-af3d5d becomes reachable: route through notme-proxy with the
   daemon's ADR-0022 gate ON, which is the only configuration where `task smoke`
   tests authorization rather than dispatch.

## Ordering

(1) is independent and small. (2) is the real work and gates (3). Doing (3)
without (2) is not possible; doing (2) without LLO's 6569de would have been
premature — that half has now landed, so the dependency is discharged.

title: build-cache/v1 is a memoize named cache — mechanism misnaming on the same wire as cloister-24c13a
description:
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:358 — "Blob identity in build-cache/v1, arena roots, substrate content addressing." The key IS the content digest, dual-verified by BlobStore.put. By the key-entails-value discriminator it is a MEMOIZE: retrieval by content digest cannot return a value differing from recomputation, and no retention policy bolted on later can change that (eviction yields a miss, never a different answer).

It has been named "cache" since inception. That is a mechanism misnaming: "cache" implies an assigned key and therefore an outstanding freshness claim, which this wire neither has nor needs.

Why this is filed separately from cloister-24c13a: same wire, different defects, different fixes. 24c13a is a digest-label bug (sha256: prefix over BLAKE3 bytes) fixable in isolation. This one only resolves once the memoize/cache boundary is pinned, so it is downstream of the mechanism-split inventory pass.

The pair is the point. Two orthogonal mislabels on one wire — an algorithm label that lies and a mechanism name that lies — found independently, an hour apart, from different directions, neither noticed for the wire lifetime. One mislabel is a bug; two is a missing step: nothing in the pipeline ever required a value to declare what it is. That is the substrate-gap evidence, not either instance alone.

Discriminator to apply (LLO, 2026-07-27): does the key determine the value? Key derived from content -> key entails value -> memoize, no extra claim. Key assigned (name, path, time) -> retained entry can disagree with recomputation -> cache, needs a freshness claim. Predicate over context -> decision -> guard, needs authorization. Checked by READING THE KEY DERIVATION, not by reasoning about eviction or TTL policy.

Inventory context: src/storage/ca-bundle-cache.ts is the correctly-named counterexample — keyed on a clock, with an explicit bounded freshness claim (refresh 4min < notme BUNDLE_MAX_AGE_MS 5min, fail-closed when stale, constants validated by lint:timing against a real notme checkout). Cloister already attaches freshness claims where needed; it just does so by hand and by comment rather than by construction.
acceptance_criteria: The build-cache/v1 wire declares its mechanism. A reader can tell from the format — not from prose — that its key is content-derived and therefore entails its value, so no freshness claim is required or implied. Resolves only after the memoize/cache boundary is pinned.

title: Taskfile sources: resolution rule is implicit and unversioned — keys silently change meaning if globs tighten
description:
Task memoizes via method: checksum over declared sources:. That is a content-derived key, so it is a genuine memoize by the key-entails-value discriminator. But the RESOLUTION RULE — what turns the glob patterns into the actual file set that gets hashed — is implicit and unversioned.

Cloister sources: are deliberately over-inclusive. Taskfile.yml states it outright: "Over-inclusive on purpose — a src/-only change skips this whole suite; any change under a listed path re-runs it." That is correct and conservative. It is also recorded only in a comment, where nothing can act on it.

The failure mode: tighten one glob and every previously-computed key silently changes meaning. Nothing records that the rule moved, so a key computed under the old rule and a key computed under the new one are indistinguishable — while attesting to different closures. Under per-skip attestation this is worse than a cache-invalidation bug: an auditor re-deriving a key has no way to know which rule to re-derive it under, so the attestation is unverifiable rather than merely stale.

Directly parallel to LLO ADR-0031 (their analysis, 2026-07-27): its closure includes "the node_defs rows those tokens resolve to", and that resolution turned out to be bare token equality — no scope, no imports, no types. Correct and conservative for their 0-false-skips-over-1786-edits result, but a future scope-aware resolver would silently change what every existing key means. Their fix was to put the resolution rule in the scheme tag (.../token-eq/v1) rather than leave it implicit. Same shape here, same fix: .../glob-closure/v1.

Priority note: latent today because nothing external consumes these keys. It becomes load-bearing the moment a skip event carrying a sources-derived digest reaches a third-party auditor, which is the memoize v1 scope of the tool-call event-plane work. Should be fixed BEFORE any such key is published, not after.

comments.text:
FOLDED into cloister-bc5640 (tool-call event plane v1) as its opening move, per operator decision 2026-07-27. Not closed — the work still has to happen, it just does not stand alone.

Reasoning for the fold: Task method:checksum is Task own mechanism. Cloister cannot change how Task computes the closure, so "version the resolution rule" cannot mean altering Task behaviour. What it can mean is DECLARING the rule in a referenceable form, so a skip event carrying a sources-derived digest names which rule produced it (.../glob-closure/v1). That declaration is inert until something references it — which makes it the first task inside the event plane rather than a standalone prerequisite.

The deadline property still holds and is the reason it goes FIRST within that work: the rule must be named before any sources-derived key reaches a third party, because after that point changing the rule silently redefines every key already in an auditor hands. Cheap now, one-way door later.
comments.author: rsry-cli

acceptance_criteria: The resolution rule that turns Taskfile sources: globs into a content-hash input closure is named and versioned (e.g. glob-closure/v1), so a change to the rule is a scheme change rather than a silent redefinition of every existing key. A key derived under one rule cannot be mistaken for a key derived under another.

title: Stale LLO generator pin is undetectable — cluster.zod.ts regenerates green against a year-old schema-bridge
description:
Reported by ley-line-open; verified here.

**The gap.** `task cluster:zod` → `schema-bridge:build` → `cargo build -p leyline-schema-bridge` against a SHA-pinned git dep. That pin is `rev = e8a501ba` (v0.7.9). The fix cloister needs (`ley-line-open-8c00c6`) is in 0.11.3. So the regen runs, exits 0, writes a `cluster.zod.ts`, and produces output from a generator five minor versions stale — with nothing anywhere reporting that.

The tell was a diff size: `cluster.zod.ts` changed by +2 lines on `feat/llo-11-3-pin`. A real regen against 0.11.3 touches every scalar field. Green build, plausible output, wrong generator.

**Why nothing caught it.** LLO's v0.11.3 release ships `leyline-*` binaries and the FFI staticlibs — no `capnpc-schema-bridge-*` plugins, and `release:target` does not build them. So the release tag is not the delivery path for the generator at all; the git rev is the only route. "We released the fix" and "consumers can get the fix" are different statements, and cloister had no way to tell them apart.

This is the same shape as the OCI address being well-formed but unpullable (cloister-195e47 / the `mutableTagReason` work): the *address* is valid, the *artifact* is not there, and the check verified the address.

**Compounding it — five pins, five revs, three copies of one crate.** `rs/*/Cargo.lock` currently resolves:

```
leyline-core          v0.4.5   rev=593ee610   (transitive via cas-ffi)
leyline-core          v0.8.0   rev=f62a5430   (transitive via fs)
leyline-core          v0.10.4  rev=45226157   (direct, in cas)
leyline-cas-ffi       v0.4.5   rev=593ee610
leyline-fs            v0.8.0   rev=f62a5430
leyline-sign          v0.7.6   rev=a6eba83a
leyline-schema-bridge v0.7.9   rev=e8a501ba
```

Three simultaneous `leyline-core` versions. At v0.11.3 all five crates are `0.11.3` under unified workspace versioning, so a single-rev bump collapses them.

LLO flagged, without verifying, that mixed revs could mean type disagreement. Worth actually checking rather than assuming either way: if a type from 0.4.5's core meets one from 0.8.0's core at any boundary, rustc treats them as distinct types even with identical definitions. They may also be genuinely independent.

**Wanted:** a rail that fails when a generator pin is stale relative to the declared LLO input version. cloister already declares `[inputs.llo] version = "0.11.3"`; nothing cross-checks that against the Cargo revs that actually produce generated output. That cross-check is the missing invariant — the declared input version and the generator rev are two statements of one fact that can disagree, which is the defect class this repo keeps finding.

title: red-team:adr-0030-2026-06-22 [C1] tenant-dispatch: verify-before-dispatch + constant-time 404 (P1)
description:
Cross-cut of bundle-isolation F1 + oracle O1 + O2 + O6. Single root cause: tenant-dispatch is BOTH a tenant-existence oracle AND a pre-auth dispatcher.

EVIDENCE:
- threat-model.md:893 (§13.7.1) claims "Router dispatches ... BEFORE handing the request to disclosure" and elsewhere implies lease verify is BEFORE dispatch. tenant-dispatch.ts:30-32 doc-comment echoes this.
- tenant-dispatch.ts:193-225 handle() does NO lease verify. Verify runs inside the target workerd. Doc lies.
- tenant-dispatch.ts:44 NOT_FOUND_BODY = "Not Found\n" (10 bytes). disclosure-cursor at src/storage/disclosure-cursor.ts:134-152 returns 256-byte zero-padded body. The comment claims "constant-time-404 invariant intact" — byte-false. Probe distinguishes 200 vs 404 by body length.
- tenant-dispatch.ts:149-164 for-loop O(N) over pathPrefix with startsWith short-circuit on first-byte divergence → measurable timing oracle (1M probes histograms cleanly).
- tenant-dispatch.ts:189-191 match() runs matchTenant; handle() runs it AGAIN. Compounds the timing leak.

ATTACK:
- Unauthenticated probe enumerates tenant table (length signal + late-row-in-table timing).
- Per-tenant DoS: tenant A absorbs full body bytes + workerd CPU before lease ever validates.

FIX (concrete):
1. tenant-dispatch.ts:44 — replace NOT_FOUND_BODY with the same CONSTANT_TIME_ERROR_BODY constant (or shape) used by disclosure-cursor.ts. Hoist to a shared module (e.g. src/wire/constant-time-404.ts) so the byte-equivalence is enforced.
2. tenant-dispatch.ts:149-164 — replace linear pathPrefix scan with a trie or longest-prefix table. Worst-case becomes O(prefix-length), independent of N.
3. tenant-dispatch.ts:189-191 — make EdgeRoute interface support a single match-and-claim (return matched row from match(), reuse in handle()) OR cache on the request object. Comment at :187 already flags the duplication.
4. ADR-0030 must decide: either dispatch is genuinely pre-auth (and we accept the body-bytes DoS, document it as residual) OR lease verify moves to the router (requires cluster-tier TrustStore on the supervisor workerd, big design lift). Pick one.

TESTS:
- test/routes/tenant-dispatch.test.ts: golden 404 byte-length test (== disclosure 404 length).
- Timing test: histogram match-time across early/late path-prefix table rows; require 95th percentile within X µs.
- Pin: TenantDispatchRoute.handle() body cannot call NOT_FOUND_BODY; must call the shared constant.

CROSS-REFS: ADR-0030 §A4 (router design), threat-model §13.7.1 (cross-tenant disclosure), §13.7.6 NEW (timing-oracle row, see synthesis report).

comments.text:
Closing — full cycle done.

**Disposition:**
- C1 / §13.7.6(a) constant-time 404 — shipped 1d03ed9 (prior session)
- §13.7.6(b) full-walk path-prefix scan, no early break — shipped b6883b0
- §13.7.6(c) match() / handle() WeakMap dedup — shipped b6883b0
- §13.7.6(d) unwired-binding warn throttle/redact — shipped 0f3f8ba (cloister-9339c0)
- §13.7.6(e) body-bytes DoS — explicit residual non-mitigation (documented in threat-model + operator guidance)

**(b) details:** `matchTenant` walks every path-prefix row regardless of which one matches. Records FIRST match (preserves table-order precedence) but does not return early. Closes the row-position oracle: latency no longer reveals where in the table a tenant lives.

Residual: per-row prefix-length-dependent micro-variance (`startsWith` + `slice` cost scales with prefix length). Below HTTP-level detection for single-digit-tenant deployments. True constant-time compare deferred.

**(c) details:** `resolveMatch()` is the new centralized compute-or-cache path through a per-route `WeakMap<Request, MatchResult|null>`. Both `match()` and `handle()` route through it. Matched requests now scan exactly once (cache populated by match(), reused by handle()).

**Tests pinned** (`test/routes/tenant-dispatch.test.ts`, +6 cases): first-match preservation, result invariance under table extension, cache presence/distinct-keys, fallback compute when handle() called without prior match().

**Threat model §13.7.6 updated**: (a)-(d) under shipped with implementation references; (e) residual with operator guidance ("front-end the router with CF WAF / cloudflared if exposed to untrusted peers"); summary-table row reflects new posture.

`task lint`: 78/78 files, 1238 tests (+6 new), all green.

title: red-team:adr-0030-2026-06-22 [C2] sharesWorkerdWith tier-confusion bypass in Inv 6 (P2)
description:

EVIDENCE:

title: red-team:adr-0030-2026-06-22 [C3] tenant-table enumeration via unwired-binding console.warn (P2)
description:
Oracle O3. tenant-dispatch.ts:208-211 console.warn emits row.name + row.binding on every unwired-binding 404. Log-aggregator-tier observer enumerates the tenant table.

EVIDENCE:
- tenant-dispatch.ts:208-211: `console.warn(\`tenant-dispatch: binding ${JSON.stringify(row.binding)} for tenant ${JSON.stringify(row.name)} is not bound...\`)` — fires per-request, no rate limit, includes both identifiers.

title: red-team:adr-0030-2026-06-22 [C4] kek-scope.validateTenantName error-shape + echo oracle (P2)
description:
Oracle O4. Two findings collapse into one: validateTenantName has 8 distinct rejection strings (categorical oracle on input shape) AND echoes the offending tenantName via JSON.stringify (confirmed-substring oracle for prober-controlled bytes).

EVIDENCE:
- kek-scope.ts:73-88 — 8 rejection cases each with distinct string ("empty", "too long", "non-ascii", "leading dot", ...). Attacker classifies any input.
- kek-scope.ts:117-120 — echoes the rejected name (potentially attacker-controlled bytes if any path from request → tenantName exists).

ATTACK:
- Combined with the disclosure-endpoint per-tenant routing, an attacker can probe arbitrary names and learn which validation class they belong to. If any code path lets an attacker influence tenantName (e.g. via SNI parsing, header injection, or future federated config) the echo becomes a substring oracle.

FIX:
1. kek-scope.ts:73-88 — collapse all 8 cases to one error: `throw new TypeError("kek-scope: invalid tenantName")`. Move the categorical reason to a debug log gated by env (so prod is one shape).
2. kek-scope.ts:117-120 — remove the JSON.stringify(name) echo. Replace with name length only or omit entirely.
3. Audit call sites of validateTenantName for any attacker-influenceable path. Document in threat-model §13.7.3 that tenantName MUST be operator-controlled, never derived from request data.

TESTS:
- test/vault/kek-scope.test.ts: assert all rejection paths throw the same error.message (use Error.message equality, not regex).
- Pin: error.message MUST NOT contain the rejected name (assert(!err.message.includes(badName))).

CROSS-REFS: threat-model §13.7.3 (KEK-scope subset property — currently aspirational, see bead C7).

title: LLO 0.11.3 PartitionSpec::address drops framing + entry order — content-address collision (ADR-0032 D2 violated)
description:
Found bumping the LLO pins to v0.11.3 (cloister-9170d0). `cargo check` passes; `cargo test -p cloister-cas` fails:

```
crates/cas/src/lib.rs:244
assertion `left != right` failed: framing must be committed to, not ignored
  left:  [51, 124, 200, 16, ...]
  right: [51, 124, 200, 16, ...]   ← identical
```

The test asserts ADR-0032 D2: the fold commits to the declared decomposition, not merely to the concatenation of its parts. Two entries differing only by framing must yield different partition addresses.

**Characterized the breadth with a temporary probe (since reverted).** `PartitionSpec::address` at rev 39e1e9b4 commits to a MULTISET OF ENTRY ADDRESSES AND NOTHING ELSE:

| varied | address changes? |
|---|---|
| `a`/`b` swapped `(0,1)`→`(1,0)` | NO |
| `b` changed outright `(0,1)`→`(0,2)` | NO |
| `(5,7)`→`(7,5)` | NO |
| **entry order** `[X,Y]`→`[Y,X]` | NO |
| entry count | yes |
| entry `addr` | yes |

So the `Entry.a` / `Entry.b` framing fields are not hashed at all, and the fold is order-insensitive.

**Why this is P0.** This is a content-addressed substrate. Two materially different decompositions — different byte ranges, different ordering — now share one address. Per CLAUDE.md, BLAKE3-256 is the substrate digest for "blob identity in build-cache/v1, arena roots". An address that does not distinguish framing means a cache lookup can return a blob assembled under a different decomposition than the one requested, and an arena root no longer pins the arrangement it names. Length-prefixed framing exists precisely to prevent this; that is the property the assertion was written to hold.

**Not a test to fix.** The assertion encodes a stated architectural property, and the shipped tree satisfied it at the previous pin. The regression is upstream in `PartitionSpec::address`.

**Open question for LLO** — whether the order-insensitivity is deliberate (a set-like commitment over entries) while the `a`/`b` omission is the actual bug, or both are unintended. Those are separable: a multiset commitment can still be framing-committed. Cloister's local `partition_address` helper only forwards to `spec.address(&es)`, so this is not a cloister-side reimplementation drift.

**Blocks** the v0.11.3 pin bump (cloister-9170d0). Everything else in that bump is clean: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` exit 0, five revs collapsed to one, three simultaneous `leyline-core` copies collapsed to one, and `cluster.zod.ts` regenerated with a real 244-line diff adding `.default(...)` per scalar (the `ley-line-open-8c00c6` fix cloister was waiting on). This single test is what stands between that bump and merge.

comments.text:
## Fixed and merged — `feat/llo-0-11-3-cargo-pins` is unblocked, and you do not need to wait for a release

`ley-line-open-afa8be` / this bead's upstream defect landed as **PR #290**, commit
**`74db5a97`** on LLO `main`. Since you pin git revs rather than releases, moving
to that commit unblocks you immediately. It is also in **v0.12.0**, tagged just
now, if you would rather take a release.

Your `address_matches_upstream_fold_for_a_known_spec` should go green: set
domains sort entries by `(addr, a, b)` and fold `addr‖a‖b`, so `glob-closure/v1`
framing variants produce distinct addresses.

## Two things that matter for your bump

**Order-insensitivity was KEPT, deliberately.** Entry enumeration order still
does not affect the address. Only framing changed. A set has no order, so
folding enumeration order in would be a malleability slot — a producer could
mint unlimited addresses for one set by permuting. If anything on your side
assumed permutation would change the address, that assumption was never valid.

ADR-0032 is genuinely ambiguous here: its operator lists children as a sequence
and commits `(addr, frame)` pairs, but never says whether set domains
canonicalize order. The sort is therefore a canonicalization choice recorded in
a decision comment at the fold, not an ADR mandate. Framing commitment, by
contrast, IS the ADR's operator as written — which is why its omission was
unambiguously a bug.

**`PARTITION_CONTEXT` stays `v1`.** The fold changed without its version tag
changing, which is normally exactly the hazard that constant exists to prevent.
It is acceptable here for one checkable reason: the buggy fold reached no tagged
release (`git tag --contains ad272d3` is empty). Your pin was at v0.7.9, far
older, so you were never in the window. Bumping would have invalidated every
`ByteStream` address, which the fix provably does not move. The reasoning is now
recorded in the code, including that a future fold change shipping in a tag MUST
bump.

## Also in v0.12.0 — the thing that stops the git-rev dance

The **generator binaries now publish**. `capnpc-schema-bridge-zod` ships per
platform, so `task schema-bridge:build` can consume a downloaded binary instead
of `cargo build` against a SHA-pinned git dep:

    curl -fsSLO .../releases/download/v0.12.0/capnpc-schema-bridge-zod-darwin-arm64
    install -m 0755 capnpc-schema-bridge-zod-darwin-arm64 ~/.local/bin/capnpc-schema-bridge-zod

The unsuffixed install name is load-bearing — capnp resolves `-o<plugin>` by
PATH-searching `capnpc-<plugin>`. That should let `cloister-9170d0`'s
stale-generator hazard be deleted at the root rather than railed around.

**Still not solved:** libraries. You would still SHA-pin `leyline-core` as a git
dep, and cargo cannot unify git deps at differing revs — which is why you had it
resolving three times at once. That needs crates.io and is tracked as
`ley-line-open-c3e8c6`.

title: ADR-0003 phase 1 hardening: BlobStore canonical-bytes API for cross-DO attestation handoff
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09 from ADR-0012 + the adversarial review of the BeadStore/TrustStore split.

## Context

ADR-0012 splits trust state (TrustStore, hypervisor-layer singleton) from bead state (BeadStore, bundle-layer per-repo). Cross-DO consistency for `peer_attestations` writes (which reference `content_hash = sha256(canonical bead bytes)`) is handled via ADR-0003's content-addressed handoff:

1. bead_create writes canonical bytes to BlobStore (CAS; idempotent).
2. BlobStore returns digest.
3. BeadStore writes row referencing digest.
4. TrustStore writes attestation referencing same digest.

Failure between steps is recoverable because step 1 is idempotent.

## What needs to be true

ADR-0003 says "Phase 1 landed." This bead checks/hardens that to ensure:

- A `BlobStore` DO class exists with `idFromName("cluster")` keying (or whatever singleton key matches TrustStore's pattern).
- BlobStore exposes a `put(canonical_bytes) → digest` API that is idempotent: same bytes → same digest, repeated calls don't double-write.
- BlobStore exposes a canonical-bytes serialization function for beads (the `bead/v1` digest shape from ADR-0003). Lives in TS so cloister-side callers can compute `content_hash` for attestation rows that reference a blob written elsewhere.
- Tests confirm: (a) idempotent put, (b) byte-stable canonical encoding, (c) digest matches what BeadStore would compute independently from the same Bead struct.

## What's potentially already there vs needs hardening

ADR-0003 has shipped Phase 1 code (per the ADR's own status), likely in `src/storage/typed-cid.ts` + `src/storage/canonical.ts`. This bead does an audit pass:

- Verify the canonical-bytes function exists and is byte-stable.
- Verify there's a DO class for content-addressed storage (or that one needs to be added).
- Verify the digest computation is deterministic (no time/random in the input).
- Add tests if missing.

## Why this bead exists separate from cloister-bdcbe7

cloister-bdcbe7 (peer_attestations) writes to TrustStore but its cross-DO transactional safety depends on this bead's deliverable. Splitting lets the audit + hardening land independently of the attestation-table work.

## Success criteria

- BlobStore DO class present + tested (or new + tested if absent).
- Canonical-bytes function exposed for callers outside the DO (so TrustStore's attestation row builder can compute digests without round-tripping).
- Idempotency property verified: `put(bytes); put(bytes)` produces same digest, single underlying row.
- Documentation / cross-link from ADR-0012's "concrete actions taken" section.

## Files (best guess; auditor may differ)

- `src/storage/typed-cid.ts` — already exists per ADR-0003 phase 1
- `src/storage/canonical.ts` — already exists per ADR-0003 phase 1
- New DO class for content-addressed storage IF one doesn't exist
- Tests under `test/storage/`

## Refs

- ADR-0003 (`docs/adr/0003-content-addressed-bead-store.md`) — the canonical source of the content-addressed design.
- ADR-0012 (`docs/adr/0012-truststore-vs-beadstore.md`) — calls this hardening out as the gating dep for cross-DO attestation writes.
- 2026-05-09 adversarial review — recommended this exact handoff pattern.

comments.text:
## Landed 2026-05-09 (commit 0ec2dff)

### What landed

`BlobStore` is now a dedicated Durable Object — singleton per cluster, reached via `env.BLOB_STORE.idFromName("cluster")`. The class extends `DurableObject` from cloudflare:workers (same pattern as TrustStore) so RPC method dispatch works cross-bundle. The DO is a thin RPC wrapper around `WorkerdBlobStore` (the existing storage class); the substrate underneath is unchanged.

### What this unblocks

The `bead_create → BlobStore → BeadStore → TrustStore` handoff that ADR-0012 promises now has a real substrate. `cloister-bdcbe7` (peer_attestations table) can proceed.

### Cross-DO consistency contract

Tested end-to-end (`test/blob-store.test.ts:108`):

> BlobStore digest of canonical bytes == beadCanonicalDigestV1(bead)

This is THE invariant ADR-0012 rests on: BeadStore (per-repo) and TrustStore (singleton) compute the same `content_hash` for the same `Bead` struct, so the attestation row references the exact blob the bead row commits to.

### Tests added (+21)

`test/storage/bead-canonical.test.ts` (12):
- versioned (v:1 preamble + bead type tag)
- byte-stable across struct-key insertion order
- labels normalized (sorted; set semantics)
- optional fields normalized (undefined → null)
- every Bead field is sensitive (no silent drops)
- updated_at included (digest commits to state at write time, not just identity)
- digest = sha256(canonical bytes) — the offline-verification contract

`test/blob-store.test.ts` (9):
- basic put/get/has
- put idempotency (3x reps produce same digest)
- re-put doesn't corrupt
- DO-computed digest matches client-side sha256 (offline verifiable)
- cross-DO consistency: BlobStore digest == beadCanonicalDigestV1
- cross-stub recovery (writer puts, reader has + gets)

421 vitest tests total, tsc clean.

### Next dependent

`cloister-bdcbe7` is now unblocked — the BlobStore DO is the substrate the math-friend recommended in ADR-0012. Once their threat model lands (cloister-bd32b1), the peer_attestations work can proceed.

title: Stale .rsry-bead-id in the canonical checkout mislabels every commit
description:
`.rsry-bead-id` is sitting in cloister's CANONICAL checkout (not an agent worktree), dated 2026-07-14, containing `cloister-a18bd3` — a bead that DOES NOT EXIST in the store.

The commit-msg hook (.git/hooks/commit-msg:29-41) auto-injects that id into any Conventional-Commits message missing a bead reference. It is doing exactly what it was designed to do; the problem is what it is reading.

MEASURED 2026-07-27: 13 commits since 2026-07-14 carry `[cloister-a18bd3]`.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. `rsry close-merged --local` scans squash-merge subjects for `[bead-id]` to auto-close the referenced bead. A stale id means either:
- nothing closes (the id resolves to no bead — today's case, a silent no-op), or
- the WRONG bead closes, if that id is ever minted for real work later.

It also makes the Golden Rule 11 convention untrustworthy in the other direction: you cannot infer from a commit which bead it belongs to, because the reference may be inherited from a file nobody remembers writing.

THE SHAPE. This is the same defect class the ART repos keep paying for: a value that does not declare whether it is still valid, and a consumer that proceeds on it without checking. The hook validates the FORM of the reference (a bracketed token) but never that it RESOLVES.

FIX OPTIONS
a) The hook validates that the injected bead exists before injecting, and refuses loudly otherwise. Turns a silent mislabel into a stop. Costs a store read per commit.
b) `.rsry-bead-id` is only honoured in a LINKED WORKTREE (git-dir != git-common-dir), never in the canonical checkout — the file was only ever meant for agent worktrees, per the hook's own comment. Cheap, no store read, and matches the documented intent.
c) Both: (b) as the structural guard, (a) as the check when it IS a worktree.

(b) is probably right on its own; the file has no business in a canonical checkout, and rosary's own pre-commit hook already uses exactly this git-dir vs git-common-dir test to decide whether it is in a worktree.

IMMEDIATE: delete `/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/cloister/.rsry-bead-id`. It is stale, and no canonical-checkout commit should be inheriting a bead id from it.

Filed from a rosary session doing cloister bead reconciliation; the reconciliation commit itself was mislabelled by this, which is how it was found.</description>

</invoke>

title: ADR-0010: Vault as scoped slices, bundles as the unit of trust, clusters as the unit of identity
description:
ADR drafted at `docs/adr/0010-vault-and-bundle-clusters.md`. Status: Proposed.

## What this ADR resolves

Three coupled questions that surfaced in the 2026-05-08 conversation:

1. **Where does the vault live?** Apache-licensed vault in `notme/vault/` should move into cloister (AGPL-3) since cloister is becoming the OSS substrate.
2. **How do tenants access it without lateral movement?** Naive vault-in-hypervisor lets one compromised handler read every secret. The slice model (capability handles scoped at instantiation) prevents this.
3. **What's the right architectural primitive for "tenant"?** Not "ToolBackend" — the actual unit is the **v8 bundle**, and a tenant is a **cluster** of bundles wired together. The `Backend` abstraction in ADR-0002 is degenerate — one cluster, one bundle, with HTTP-forward "backends" that are really external clusters' bundles.

## Three coupled primitives

- **Bundle**: a unit of v8 isolation. Worker entry + declared routes + vault slice + service bindings + DO namespaces. Today's "cloister-router," "notme-identity," "cloister-companion" are bundles.
- **Cluster**: a set of bundles sharing one Interlace actor identity. Inter-bundle = service bindings (intra-cluster, unforgeable). Inter-cluster = Interlace + CF Tunnel.
- **VaultSliceGrant**: a path-globbed scope a bundle can read/write. Issued by the manifest runtime at boot via HMAC token; bundle never sees the unrestricted vault.

## KEK derivation

`KEK = HKDF(IKM=SigningAuthority.master_pubkey, salt="cloister-vault-kek-v1", info=cluster.name||":vault-kek")`. **No env-var bootstrap.** Cluster has one root (Ed25519 master, born-in-CF in `SigningAuthority` DO from notme). Rotation via Signet epoch (revocation.ts). One audit trail.

## License

Apache-2.0 → AGPL-3 lift is legal (we own the copyright; one-way move is clean). notme stays Apache 2.0; notme drops its vault dependency in Phase 5 (uses small ad-hoc sealed-DO helper for its OAuth-token wrap).

## 5-phase migration plan

1. **OSS-readiness sweep** — CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY/CODE_OF_CONDUCT/CLAUDE/AGENTS.md, .github/workflows, public README polish. Cloister has 0 deployments + 0 external commits, so no backwards-compat to maintain.
2. **Lift `notme/vault/` → `cloister/src/vault/`** under AGPL-3, NOT wired in yet.
3. **Add Bundle/Cluster/VaultSliceGrant grammar** to `manifest/cloister.capnp`, mirror in `src/manifest/types.ts`, wrap existing manifest in single `cluster:{bundles:[router-bundle]}`. Runtime rewrites to instantiate per-cluster.
4. **Wire vault DO + slice tokens.** KEK derivation from SigningAuthority. Slice handles given to bundles at boot.
5. **Migrate env-var bindings to vault paths.** Sweep `LLO_MCP_URL`, `MACHE_MCP_URL`, `ROSARY_MCP_URL`, `SIGNET_URL`, `COMPANION_URL`, `INTERLACE_MASTER_PUBKEY` → vault entries with bundle-scoped slices. Drop env-var fields.
6. **notme cleanup** — drop vault dep, replace with small in-DO sealed helper.

## Impact on in-flight beads

- **cloister-bd9b5f** (just shipped — `.well-known/interlace/`): emits master pubkey via `env[pubkeyBinding]`. Will be re-targeted to `slice.read("identity/master/pubkey")` in Phase 5.
- **cloister-bd7770** (lease middleware): originally specced to read pubkey from env; will read from vault slice instead. No architectural change to the bead, just the read path.
- **cloister-e195ea** (revocation bundle refresh): same — fetches via service binding + reads vault entries.
- **ADR-0007's `actor` block** currently lives on `Gateway`; will migrate to `Cluster` in Phase 3. Mechanical capnp ordinal shuffle.

## Lateral-movement threat model (the core question)

User correctly flagged: vault-in-hypervisor is a lateral-movement risk if vault access is unscoped. ADR resolves this with the slice model:

- Manifest runtime holds the unrestricted vault interface for the duration of `instantiate(manifest)` only.
- Each bundle gets a `VaultSlice` handle bound to its capnp-declared scope at construction.
- Bundle never sees the parent vault — closure scope + v8 isolate boundary keeps the unrestricted ref unreachable.
- Vault DO requires a slice token (HMAC) on every read. Token encodes scope + mode + bundle name. Forgery requires the KEK (= Signet master derivative).
- Cross-language ground truth: token verification at the DO. Closure-based unforgeability is the v8-side mechanism; in Rust companion it would be private struct fields + move semantics.

## Success criteria

- `docs/adr/0010-vault-and-bundle-clusters.md` lands at status Proposed (done — this bead tracks acceptance).
- Each phase has its own implementation bead in this decade.
- ADR-0007 implementation beads (bd9b5f, bd7770, e195ea) get rerouted to vault slices once Phase 4 lands; sweep beads tracked separately.
- ADR-0010 moves to Accepted when Phases 1-3 are in flight (the architectural commitment is enough; full migration can take longer).

## Files
- `docs/adr/0010-vault-and-bundle-clusters.md` (this ADR, drafted)

## Open questions captured in the ADR
- Glob grammar — POSIX-style single-component wildcards for v1; revisit later
- External-bundle marker — `contentHash=""` + `externalEndpoint` field; formalized at Phase 3
- Slice-token revocation — boot-only for v1; live revocation deferred

title: Lift notme/vault → cloister/vault (copy-not-move; notme keeps its copy for now)
description:
Per ADR-0010 cloister-97610c. **Scope narrowed 2026-05-09**: copy-not-move. notme keeps its `vault/` directory unchanged; cloister gets a self-contained AGPL-3 copy with origin attribution. Avoids breaking notme during the OSS prep; consolidation deferred until a real consumer asks for it.

## Source files to lift (notme/vault/ → cloister/vault/, copy)

- `src/vault.ts` — credential storage + validation + access checks
- `src/crypto.ts` — KEK/DEK envelope (AES-GCM, HKDF)
- `src/handler.ts` — request handler + audit log builder
- `src/worker.ts` — Worker entry point
- `src/__tests__/vault.test.ts`
- `src/__tests__/vault-security.test.ts`
- `src/__tests__/vault-adversarial.test.ts`
- `src/__tests__/encryption.test.ts`
- `src/__tests__/worker.test.ts`
- `wrangler.toml.example`

## Wiring into cloister

`notme/vault/` has no `package.json` of its own — it relies on `notme/worker/tsconfig.json` and `notme/worker/vitest.config.ts` to compile/test the vault sources via include paths. Copy the same pattern in cloister:

- Extend `cloister/tsconfig.json` `include` with `vault/src/**/*.ts`
- Extend `cloister/vitest.config.ts` test paths with `vault/src/__tests__/**/*.test.ts`

This keeps the lift to a literal directory copy; no new package.json or workspace member needed. If vault grows enough to warrant its own deploy lifecycle later, splitting into a separate workspace package is a follow-up bead.

## Re-license

- SPDX header on every source file: `// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later`
- Top-level `cloister/vault/NOTICE` documenting Apache-2.0 origin from `agentic-research/notme`, copyright (c) the same author. Required per Apache 2.0 §4(c).

## What this bead does NOT do

- Does NOT remove `notme/vault/` (deferred — see notme-9af5dd update).
- Does NOT wire vault into cloister's manifest as a Bundle (that's ADR-0010 Phase 3).
- Does NOT generate slice tokens or KEK-from-Signet derivation (Phase 4).
- Does NOT replace any env-var bindings (Phase 5).

This bead is JUST the lift + relicense. Code in `cloister/vault/`, AGPL-3, isolated, tests pass. The vault DO is not yet reachable from cloister's manifest runtime.

## Cross-repo coupling

**None for this bead.** notme is untouched. notme-9af5dd (notme-side cleanup) is deferred to "when consolidation has a reason."

## Success criteria

- `cloister/vault/src/` mirrors `notme/vault/src/` byte-for-byte (modulo SPDX headers).
- `cloister/vault/NOTICE` documents Apache-2.0 origin per §4(c).
- `cloister/vault/wrangler.toml.example` copied.
- Cloister's tsconfig + vitest config pulls in vault sources.
- Vault tests pass: `task lint` covers them.
- No new imports from `cloister/src/` into `cloister/vault/` (clean isolation).

## Files
- `vault/` (new directory, ~10 source files)
- `vault/NOTICE` (new)
- `vault/wrangler.toml.example` (new, copied)
- `tsconfig.json` (extend `include`)
- `vitest.config.ts` (extend test paths)

title: config.capnp ↔ wrangler.toml bindings have drifted — 6 trust-surface vars exist only on the CF path
description:
Found during the manumation audit. CLAUDE.md:25 states these "must stay in sync"; ADR-0001:70 records it as a known weakness ("must be kept in sync with wrangler.toml **manually** — two sources of truth for bindings"). Nothing enforces it, and it has drifted.

Present in `wrangler.toml`, absent from `config.capnp`, and **read in `src/`**:

```
INTERLACE_ROOT_PUBKEY           read in 3 src files
INTERLACE_MASTER_PUBKEY         read in 3 src files
INTERLACE_DISCLOSURE_HMAC_KEY   read in 1
RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY             read in 1
RECEIPT_EPOCH                   read in 1
CANONICAL_HOURS_MCP_URL         read in 2
```

`config.capnp` has zero `fromEnvironment` entries, so these are not supplied by another mechanism — the workerd-local path runs code reading env vars that its config never provides.

Five names go the other way (`COMPANION_MCP`, `MACHE_MCP`, `LSP_MCP`, `ROSARY_MCP`, `KEK_HELPER`) but those look legitimate rather than drift: workerd uses service bindings where CF uses `*_MCP_URL` vars over HTTP. That asymmetry is a difference in binding MECHANISM, not a missing binding — a rail must model it rather than flag it.

**Severity.** Not an auth bypass: per ADR-0053 absent authority enforces and then fails closed at `resolveCABundle` with `-32005`. The consequence is that the entire trust surface — lease gate, disclosure HMAC, receipt signing — cannot be exercised on the workerd path at all. `task serve:local` and `task smoke` therefore cannot cover it, which is a testability gap on precisely the surface the threat model treats as the contract.

**Wanted:** a `lint:binding-parity` rail comparing the two surfaces, with a declared table of legitimate mechanism differences (service-binding vs URL-var) so the exceptions are explicit and greppable rather than implied. Same shape as the existing `lint-allow-*` markers.

Part of the manumation cluster: [[cloister-846228]] (hand-maintained test list), [[cloister-9170d0]] (Cargo pins vs declared input version). Distinct from those in that it is not schema-derivable — `config.capnp` and `wrangler.toml` are two hand-authored files with no common generator, so this one needs a rail rather than elimination.
acceptance_criteria: A rail fails when a binding read in src/ is declared in wrangler.toml but not config.capnp (or vice versa) without an explicit declared exception. Verified by: run `task lint` on the current tree and confirm it fails naming the six vars; add the declared-exception entries for the service-binding/URL-var pairs and confirm it then passes; introduce a new unpaired binding and confirm it fails again.

title: ADR-0024 Phase 8 revisit condition has fired — decide the capability registry now the matchmaker has landed
description:
Filed 2026-07-28. Not a gap — a deferral whose trigger has now fired.

## The original decision

ADR-0024 Phase 8 (capability registry), deferred 2026-06-20 per cred-iso audit
R-5 (`cloister-12bf80`):

    Original spec: `/.well-known/cloister-capabilities/v1/` lists this
    capability. Disposition: held pending ADR-0027 matchmaker. The matchmaker
    surfaces capability discovery via the input-resolution path (`[inputs.*]`
    in `cluster.toml`), which makes a separate `/.well-known/` lookup likely
    redundant. Revisit when the matchmaker lands or when a concrete consumer
    needs a stable well-known surface independent of input resolution.

A well-made deferral: reason, date, and a named revisit condition.

## The condition has fired — half of it

The matchmaker HAS landed. `scripts/capability-matchmaker.mjs` is on main and
runs in the lint gate.

But the substance of the argument has not changed, and this is the part worth
weighing: per CLAUDE.md, **no input declares a lattice yet**. So
discovery-via-input-resolution currently has zero traffic. Standing up a
`/.well-known/` surface now would advertise a capability set that nothing
consumes, through a mechanism nothing exercises — building the second discovery
path before the first has a single user.

## Why this is worth deciding rather than leaving

The deferral is recorded in ADR-0024's phase list, which is not where anyone
looks. Meanwhile `docs/plans/credential-isolation-capability.md` cites
`leyline-schema-spec/capability-discovery/v1/` as a follow-up to file, reading
as "someone forgot" rather than "someone decided". That mismatch is how a
deliberate deferral gets re-litigated from scratch, or worse, quietly
implemented by someone who assumed it was an oversight.

## Map of the adjacent work, so it is not confused for this

Four distinct concerns; three are owned, one is not:

| concern | owner |
|---|---|
| capability GRANT representation (Action/Resource/Constraint/Context, `urn:signet:cap:`) | signet — `docs/design/010-semantic-capability-protocol.md`, `pkg/signet/capability.go` |
| capability IDENTIFIER lanes (which of three schemes to write) | ley-line-open — `schema-spec/_capability-mapping.md` (ADR-0028 crosswalk, `cloister-224917`) |
| capability MATCHMAKING (`provides`/`requires` resolution) | cloister — `scripts/capability-matchmaker.mjs` (ADR-0027) |
| capability DISCOVERY (endpoint response shape) | nobody |

Searching all of LLO, notme and signet for `*capabilit*` finds the first two and
nothing resembling a discovery response format. "Capability discovery moved to
LLO" is the near-miss to avoid: the adjacent thing landed, this did not.

## The decision to make

Either (a) confirm the deferral stands and say so where a reader will find it —
the second half of ADR-0024's argument still holds while the lattice has no
inhabitants; or (b) if a concrete consumer now needs a well-known surface
independent of input resolution, name that consumer and spec the response shape.

Do NOT implement it without (b)'s consumer. ADR-0027's matchmaker is already a
gate with no traffic; a second unexercised discovery surface would compound
that.

comments.text:
Operator: "I mean we need it don't we?" — yes, and the answer sharpens the
decision. We need capabilities ADVERTISED; we very likely do not need a new
endpoint.

## What already ships

`/.well-known/mcp-registry/v0.1/servers` (ADR-0016, cloister-a30e40) serves the
standard MCP Registry shape, enumerating cloister's backends as server.json
documents. Server and tool discovery is DONE, in a form host applications
already consume.

What it does not carry is SUBSTRATE capabilities — `cloister/credential-
isolation/v1`, `cloister/confinement/v1`. Those are not servers or tools. A peer
asking "does this cloister mediate credentials?" cannot learn it from a server
list, which is the real gap.

## The extension point exists

`src/routes/well-known-mcp-registry.ts` already builds a `_meta` envelope
(`RegistryEnvelopeMeta`, `buildMetaEnvelope`, line ~239), and the route's own
comment notes the Registry spec RESERVES `_meta` for registries to extend.

So capabilities can ride the existing endpoint. No new well-known surface, no
second discovery path, no new URL to version and defend.

## This corrects ADR-0024's stated reason

Phase 8 deferred on the grounds that "the matchmaker surfaces capability
discovery via the input-resolution path, which makes a separate /.well-known/
lookup likely redundant."

The CONCLUSION holds; the REASON does not. The matchmaker runs at BUILD time
over pinned refs in cluster.toml. It answers nothing at runtime, and a peer or
host application has no access to it at all. Redundancy is real but comes from
the registry envelope, not the matchmaker.

Worth fixing in the ADR amendment, because a right conclusion resting on a wrong
reason survives only until someone checks the reason — and the next person to
check would conclude discovery IS needed as a separate surface.

## Revised decision shape

Not "build or defer a capability registry" but:

1. Emit declared capabilities into the existing registry `_meta` envelope.
2. Do NOT stand up `/.well-known/cloister-capabilities/v1/`.
3. Keep ADR-0024's consumer bar for anything beyond (1): a separate surface
   still needs a named consumer that the registry envelope cannot serve.

(1) is small and has an obvious first inhabitant — `credential-isolation/v1` is
implemented, declared in cluster.toml as a route, and currently invisible to any
external reader.

Caveat worth carrying: per CLAUDE.md no input declares a `provides`/`requires`
lattice yet, so what (1) advertises today is cloister's OWN capabilities rather
than a resolved cluster-wide set. That is still strictly more than zero, and it
does not require the lattice to have inhabitants first.

title: lint:spec-citation covers the specs cloister CONSUMES, not the one it PUBLISHES
description:
scripts/lint-spec-citation.mjs polices leyline-schema-spec/... citations — 36 of them, resolving into LLO's checkout. It contains ZERO references to interlace-spec. Cloister therefore proves its pointers into the spec it CONSUMES resolve, and proves nothing about pointers into the spec it PUBLISHES.

That is the more expensive direction. interlace-spec/ is cloister-owned and its README tells third parties (notme, signet) 'if you reach the same digests on the test vectors in test-vectors/, you are conformant.' A dangling pointer in a spec other repos implement against costs more than a dangling pointer in cloister's own prose.

## The asymmetry has already bitten
interlace-spec/0.2.0-draft/RECEIPTS.md §7 line 751:

    The following test vectors are required in
    `interlace-spec/0.2.0/test-vectors/`. Each implementation **MUST**
    reproduce them byte-equal.

- The path says 0.2.0/; the directory on disk is 0.2.0-draft/.
- 0.2.0-draft/test-vectors/ exists but holds only url-canonicalization/ — none of the receipt vectors that MUST names.
- 0.2.0-draft has no VECTORS.sha256 at all. 0.1.0 does.

An unfinished draft is fine. A normative MUST written as though already satisfied, pointing at a version string that does not exist, is the thing a rail would have caught on the day it was written.

## Scoping note (do not overstate)
Of the four citations to 'interlace-spec/0.2.0' without -draft, TWO are domain-separation string constants — SHA-256("interlace-spec/0.2.0 genesis batch") — and are correct as literals, not paths. One is a forward-looking recommendation in docs/cross-repo-audit.md. Only RECEIPTS.md §7 is a real dangling citation. The rail must distinguish a path citation from a string literal, which is the same lesson lint:schema-claim learned (a mention is not a claim).

## Related
cloister-7c9312 / cloister-7f4c45 are the mirror image: cloister does not verify it OBEYS the specs it consumes. This bead is that cloister does not verify its own published spec's pointers RESOLVE. Same discipline, both directions.
acceptance_criteria: The citation rail resolves interlace-spec/... references as well as leyline-schema-spec/..., with a companion test asserting the shipped tree satisfies it; the RECEIPTS.md version-string mismatch is fixed or explicitly marked unresolved-by-design.

title: ADR + binding: cloister Worker → external dolt-sql-server (bd substrate adoption)
description:
## Context

The rosary LLM (2026-06-23 session) flipped its ADR-0012 reading after re-reading the `bd` README: bd ships with **socket-mode dolt-sql-server** that handles concurrent writers and is sandbox-friendly. That dissolves the previous "rosary is Rust, can't embed Dolt" blocker. The corrected ADR-0012 direction:

> Adopt `bd` as the shared issue-tracking substrate (server-mode-over-socket); rosary drives the bd CLI + connects to the Dolt server via MySQL. cloister Workers via service binding. Stop minting parallel IDs; stop reading the store directly.

The cloister wrinkle: cloister is a v8-isolate/workerd hypervisor. The Worker can't embed bd OR Dolt — no local FS for `.beads/embeddeddolt/`, no in-isolate process to run a sql-server. **The only path is a service binding from cloister-router → external dolt-sql-server, with cloister mediating credentials.** That's literally what cloister's `cloister/credential-isolation/v1` capability (ADR-0024) was built for.

This bead captures the cloister-side design work; depends on rosary ADR-0012 landing first.

## Scope

1. **ADR-0033** (next free number per `docs/STATUS.md`): cloister Worker → external dolt-sql-server binding. Reads:
   - Topology decision (TCP service binding via `external` per ADR-0030 §A2 patterns vs UDS via ADR-0023 host-path resolution)
   - Authentication shape: MySQL auth via vault-injected credential (ADR-0013 slice-grant) — credential is a MySQL user/password OR a TLS client cert (TBD)
   - Trust boundary: cloister-router → dolt-sql-server is INSIDE the cluster trust boundary (analogous to BeadStore DO RPC today); auth is "the substrate proves it's me" not "the substrate verifies external identity"
   - Failure mode: dolt-sql-server unreachable → cloister returns 503 with the same constant-shape response as other substrate-unavailable paths (§13.x)

2. **Manifest extension**:
   - New `Backend.kind` variant: `mysqlProxy` or rename of existing `serviceBinding` with a sub-typed wire protocol marker
   - Or: declare `dolt-sql-server` as a config.capnp `external` service (per ADR-0030 §A2) and bind via existing service-binding mechanisms — no new backend kind needed
   - Pick whichever has less schema churn

3. **vaultProxy integration**:
   - The MySQL credential lives in vault (ADR-0024 service registry). Bind `[vault.services.dolt]` with the upstream URL pointing at the external service.
   - Vault DO injects credentials, fetcher forwards to dolt-sql-server. Plaintext credential never leaves the DO.

4. **Substrate-property lint extension** (`lint-bundle-isolation.mjs`):
   - New invariant: any bundle with a `dolt-sql-server` binding must declare it under `holdsCredential` (Inv 2 already covers this; verify it captures the MySQL credential kind).

## Open questions (defer to ADR draft)

- TCP vs UDS for the dolt-sql-server connection? UDS preferred per ADR-0023 + ADR-0030 §A1 pattern, but bd may default to TCP.
- TLS termination? If TLS, where does the CA bundle come from? (See §15 trust-anchor-helper precedent.)
- Per-bundle vault DO instances (ADR-0021): is each bundle's bd connection a separate credential, or do they share one cluster-wide MySQL user? Sharing is simpler; separating is the ADR-0013 slice-grant story.
- What about workerd-local dev? `wrangler dev` doesn't have a real service binding network — fall back to a stubbed MySQL fetcher? Or require `task dev:bd-server` to spin up a local dolt-sql-server?

## Dependencies

- **Blocks on**: rosary ADR-0012 rewrite (the substrate adoption decision itself). Don't draft this ADR until rosary's lands; otherwise we're designing against a moving target.
- **Sub-beads to spawn from this**: notme-side credential mint (filed separately in notme/), implementation epic, lint-bundle-isolation Inv extension.

## Tracking

- Parent: rosary's ADR-0012 rewrite (not yet filed in rosary tracker — filed-via-conversation 2026-06-23)
- Related cloister ADRs: ADR-0024 (cred-iso/v1), ADR-0021 (per-bundle vault DOs), ADR-0030 (multi-workerd substrate), ADR-0023 (host-path resolution / UDS).
- Threat-model touchpoint: new §13.x entry for the dolt-sql-server connection trust boundary.

title: [bd7770 follow-up] WASM cert-chain verify + claims parsing for ephemeral Signet certs
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09 from cloister-bd7770 Phase 1 (lease middleware substrate). The middleware ships header parsing, canonical bytes, scope grammar, lease counter UPSERT, and JSON-RPC error builders — but the actual cert verification is stubbed with `ERR_CERT_NOT_IMPL` because the WASM verifier (`leyline_verify` in `rs/crates/sign/src/ffi.rs`) doesn't yet expose:

1. **Cert-chain verification**: take an ephemeral cert DER + a master pubkey, return ok/error.
2. **Claims parsing**: extract `peer_fingerprint`, `scope`, `epoch`, `not_before`, `not_after`, and the ephemeral pubkey (SubjectPublicKeyInfo) from the cert's X.509 + custom-OID extensions (`1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.*` arc).

Without these, the lease middleware can't actually verify a cert. The Phase 1 stub in `src/routes/lease-middleware.ts` documents the full flow + returns ERR_CERT_NOT_IMPL from the stub points (fail closed).

## Two implementation options

### Option A — extend the WASM crate (recommended)

Add new FFI exports to `rs/crates/sign/src/ffi.rs`:

```rust
/// Verify cert is signed by master_pubkey + write parsed claims
/// (peer_fp, scope, epoch, not_before, not_after, ephemeral_spki) as a
/// flat structure (e.g. JSON or capnp) into claims_out_buf.
/// Returns claims byte length on success, -1 on failure.
pub unsafe extern "C" fn leyline_verify_cert_chain(
    cert_der_ptr: *const u8, cert_der_len: usize,
    master_pubkey_ptr: *const u8, master_pubkey_len: usize,
    claims_out_buf: *mut u8, claims_out_len: usize,
) -> i32;
```

The Rust crate already has X.509 parsing via `x509-cert` + Ed25519 verify via `ed25519-dalek`. The work is ~100 LOC of glue + a new TS wrapper in `src/wire/signet-verify.ts`.

### Option B — TS X.509 parser

Use a TypeScript X.509 library (e.g. `@peculiar/x509` — already used by notme) to parse + verify in pure TS. crypto.subtle has Ed25519 verify in workerd. Fewer Rust changes but adds a TS dep. Less code reuse with the Rust companion / ll CLI.

Recommend Option A for code reuse and substrate-portability (per ADR-0009).

## Wire format for claims

Pick one and document:
- **JSON** (simplest): `{"peer_fp":"sha256:...","scope":"bead_create:*","epoch":7,"not_before":1700000000,"not_after":1700000300,"ephemeral_spki":"<base64>"}`. Parse on the TS side. ~50 bytes-of-glue.
- **capnp** (consistent with rest of cloister): define a `CertClaims` struct in `wire/cloister.capnp`, encode in Rust via the wasm output buffer, decode on TS side. More work but matches the leyline-net wire idiom.

Recommend JSON for v1 (simpler, claims are small) — if the wire format becomes load-bearing, migrate to capnp.

## Wiring back into bd7770's middleware

After this lands, the stub in `src/routes/lease-middleware.ts:verifyAndUpsertLease` (currently returns `ERR_CERT_NOT_IMPL`) gets replaced with the actual flow:

1. Call new TS wrapper `verifyCertChain(certDer, masterPubkey)` → returns `CertClaims | null`.
2. Check `isCertEpochCurrent(claims.epoch, bundle)` (already in cloister-e195ea).
3. Parse the ephemeral SPKI as a CryptoKey via `crypto.subtle.importKey`.
4. Verify the request signature: `crypto.subtle.verify("Ed25519", ephemeralKey, sig, canonical)`.
5. Check `claims.not_before * 1000 <= nowMs <= claims.not_after * 1000`.
6. Check `scopeAllows(claims.scope, deriveRequestScope(...))` (already in lease-middleware).
7. UPSERT lease counter (already in lease-middleware).

All the helpers exist; this bead just plugs in the actual cert verification.

## Success criteria

- New FFI export(s) added to `leyline-sign` (Option A) or TS X.509 parser added (Option B).
- TS wrapper `verifyCertChain` exposed from `src/wire/signet-verify.ts`.
- Round-trip test: a cert minted by notme's `mintBridgeCertPair` (or a Rust-side fixture) verifies + claims parse correctly.
- Bad-master-pubkey, expired cert, wrong-extensions inputs all reject.
- bd7770's stub points are replaced with actual logic; ERR_CERT_NOT_IMPL goes away.

## Refs

- bd7770 — provides the middleware skeleton this bead completes.
- notme/worker/src/cert-authority.ts — the cert-mint side; defines the X.509 extension OID arc (`1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.*`).
- ADR-0007 — defines what the lease middleware does end-to-end.
- rs/crates/sign/src/cert.rs — existing X.509 parser; add cert-chain verify alongside.

## Files (best guess)

- `rs/crates/sign/src/cert.rs` (extend)
- `rs/crates/sign/src/ffi.rs` (new exports)
- `src/wire/signet-verify.ts` (extend)
- `src/routes/lease-middleware.ts` (un-stub)
- `test/wire/signet-verify.test.ts` (new tests)
- `test/routes/lease-middleware.test.ts` (integration tests)
